cards.title: Pre-session checklist
cards.body:
- [ ] Re-read the **Act** you are in and its session list.
- [ ] Write down the three most likely things the party will do next. Read the matching **IF THEY…** boxes.
- [ ] Choose one **faction move**: something a faction does off-screen this week. Write it down.
- [ ] Choose one **rumour** from Part 11 that the party can overhear.
- [ ] Know the names, voices, and one secret of the three NPCs most likely to appear.
- [ ] Check the **Toll Tracker** (Appendix B.1) so you know who has paid what.
- [ ] Check the **Tithe Clock** (Part 2.12) and the **Faction Clock** (Appendix B.3).
- [ ] Decide how you will end the session. End on a question, not a resolution.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 1: "We want to kill the Quiet Chancellor right now."
cards.body:
> **SAY:** "You could try. She's surrounded by Hushmen and Dawn Order knights, and every glove on her hands is silence-stone. Are you sure?"

**DO:** Let them try, if they insist. Use the Strike encounter (Session 23) or the summit fight (Session 24). Maudrin will not die easily. She has allies and a favour she can call in. Foreshadow a successor with a rumour: "The Court has a second Chancellor waiting in the wings: a cousin named Tristan Vesk, who has been quietly writing to the Court's council."

**IF THEY…**
- **…succeed:** The Court splinters. Factions fight each other in Hallowmere. The party is hunted by both sides. Tristan Vesk becomes the Court's new Chancellor and offers the party a deal for the Key. Adjust Act V: Tristan does not have the Key, but he knows where it is.
- **…fail:** Maudrin is merciful, once. She sends them back to Pellmoor with a warning, and she does not forgive them a second time.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 2: "We want to ring every bell right now."
cards.body:
> **SAY:** "You can't. The Tongues are scattered across Corvane, and each bell is guarded. What do you want to ring first?"

**DO:** Make the party earn each Tongue. Use the Tongue table (Part 2.10) to remind them where each one is. Each bell rung makes the Court more aggressive, Use the Court as that session's one faction tick.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 3: "We want to go straight to the Seventh Bell."
cards.body:
> **SAY:** "You don't know where the Seventh is, and the Key is with Maudrin. You'll need to find both. Would you like to go to the Tor first, or to the Court?"

**DO:** Allow them to go, but make them pay. The Seventh is at the bottom of 100 steps (Session 25), and the Key is required to ring it. If they find another way down, the Hush notices them early, and the lullaby begins to crack. Advance the Hush Cult's Faction Clock.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 4: "We want to steal the Key from Maudrin."
cards.body:
> **SAY:** "Maudrin carries the Key on a chain around her neck, in a silence-stone case. Who among you can make a bell's sound disappear?"

**DO:** Let the party plan. Good plans should work. The best routes are: the Strike (Session 23), where the Key is in Maudrin's hands during a fight; Ansel Quay's knowledge of her routes (Part 5.2, #21); and Tonework that cancels tones (*Silence*).

**Important:** Since Session 22, the Key is not in Hallowmere. If the party goes back to Hallowmere to rob the Court's palace, they find only the Court's Tithe-Ledger, Calla's shelf, and Ansel Quay. Describe the empty vault, and let the emptiness be the clue.

**IF THEY…**
- **…succeed:** Maudrin realizes in one day, and sends everyone after them. The party now carries the Key, which is dangerous to hold. Each night, the Key hums louder, and a Ringer who holds it begins to dream the lullaby.
- **…fail:** Hushmen capture one party member. Maudrin offers to trade them for the Key. A DC 15 Insight check reveals whether she is bluffing. She is not.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 5: "We want to make a deal with Maudrin."
cards.body:
> **SAY:** "She's listening. What do you want, and what are you willing to give?"

**DO:** Maudrin's bargains are always real, and always incomplete. She keeps her word about the thing you bargain for, and she breaks every other promise. Track every deal in the Bargain Log (Appendix B.2).

**Typical Maudrin deals:**
- Safe passage in exchange for one Tongue.
- A memory restored in exchange for another memory given to the Tithe.
- The freedom of a prisoner in exchange for a secret.
- A Court pension in exchange for silence about the Quiet Night.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 6: "We want to ring the bells and not pay the Toll."
cards.body:
> **SAY:** "The Toll is part of the bell. You can't ring it without giving something up. What do you want to give?"

**DO:** Hold firm. The Toll is the core of the campaign. If players refuse to choose, the DM chooses (Part 2.7). Choose something painful but not catastrophic: a Sense, a Fear, or a Year. Give the player the choice whenever you can.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 7: "We want to kill Ila Harrow, Jonah Bray, or another child."
cards.body:
> **SAY:** "They're children. Why would you want to hurt them?"

**DO:** Shut this down at the table. Most groups treat harm to children as a Line. If it is a Line for your group, do not let it become a central feature of the story. The party will face consequences from the Court and from the villagers, and the children's families will seek vengeance. If a child is in danger, have an NPC step in: Mother Sallow, Ilam Bray, or Bet Ostrow.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 8: "We want to ignore the main plot and explore, make money, or go on side quests."
cards.body:
> **SAY:** "That's fine. Corvane is big. What do you do first?"

**DO:** Let them. Corvane has plenty of side content (Part 11.6). The main plot keeps moving: the Court's Tithes, the Hushmen patrols, the Silence's slow unravelling. Advance one faction clock each session. If the party is away for three or more sessions, have the Court make a dramatic move in Pellmoor: take Mother Sallow, burn the ledger, Tithe the village.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 9: "We want to join the Quiet Court."
cards.body:
> **SAY:** "That's an unusual choice. The Court values order above all things. What do you bring to the table?"

**DO:** Let them. This is a strong route. They gain power, safety, and access to the Tithe. They will also be asked to Tithe people, including their own friends. Give them the Tithe-Ledger as a tool, and ask every session for one name they record. The Court's ideal is Order. Ask the player: "Will you still believe in Order when it is asked of someone you love?"

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 10: "We want to become Bellwrights."
cards.body:
> **SAY:** "The Bellwrights are hunted, and they have few resources. They'll need proof of your skill. Can you make a bell?"

**DO:** Let them learn Tonework (Bellwright, Part 2.6). The Bellwrights' ideal is Memory. Give them an apprentice: Wren Caddock, Ila Harrow, or Bet Ostrow. The Bellwrights ask them to ring a small bell as a test. The first ringing should always be a small one, with a small Toll.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 11: "We want to negotiate with the Drowned Choir, the Stilled, the Sleepless, or the Hush."
cards.body:
> **SAY:** "They're not like the living. They don't negotiate the way you do. What do you want to ask them?"

**DO:** Let them. Non-human factions can negotiate, but they ask strange things in return. The Drowned Choir wants a true memory of the dead. The Stilled want to move. The Sleepless want a dream of their own. The Hush wants rest.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 12: "We want to burn the Bone Archive, the Hall of Tithes, or the whole city."
cards.body:
> **SAY:** "That's a lot of books. And a lot of people. Are you sure?"

**DO:** If it is clear they mean it, let them. The city responds with a massive Hushmen sweep and a Dawn Order response. The party is hunted across the Ninefold Shore. The Blanks are freed, and some of them are permanently changed by the fire. The Tithe Clock jumps to 12 ticks immediately. Adjust Acts IV and V to be more dangerous, and make the ending darker.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 13: "We want to turn on each other."
cards.body:
> **SAY:** "Corvane is full of people who want things from you. Your friends may want something too. Who is hiding something from the party?"

**DO:** Use the Secrets. Each party member should have one secret on the Toll Tracker, which only the DM and the player see. Let the player choose whether to reveal it. If a party member betrays the group, use the betrayal to drive the story, but make sure the betrayed player still has a meaningful role. Do not take away a player's character.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 14: "We want to rest for a long time."
cards.body:
> **SAY:** "You can rest, but the Long Dusk doesn't wait. Every night you rest in a Court city, the Tithe-quota grows, and the Hush gets a little louder."

**DO:** Let them rest, and advance the Tithe Clock (Part 2.12). At 6 ticks, the Court makes a major move. At 12, the Silence spreads to the city.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 15: "We want to talk to the bells, the Silence, or the gods directly."
cards.body:
> **SAY:** "The bells can't speak. But the Hush can, and so can the Librarian. And the Dreamer, if you're brave enough to ask."

**DO:** Use the Librarian (Act II) and the Hush (Act IV, Branch B). Both answer one question for each true memory or true sacrifice. Make their answers true but partial. Do not give the party the whole truth early.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 16: "We want to use a Toll for something else."
cards.body:
> **SAY:** "The Toll is always personal. It's what you give. What do you want to buy with it?"

**DO:** Let them spend Tolls on other things, but the Toll should always cost the character something real. A memory can buy protection, a favour from an NPC, a ritual, or a key. Make the price visible and record it.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 17: "We want to leave Corvane or find another world."
cards.body:
> **SAY:** "There's nowhere else. Corvane is all there is. But there is the sea, the Ninefold Shore, and the edge of the world where the dream grows thin. Do you want to go there?"

**DO:** Use the Edge of the Dream (Part 11.7). It is a terrifying and beautiful place. Let the party explore it for one session. It can serve as a pre-Act V encounter or as an alternative ending.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 18: "We want to fight a dragon, a god, or a monster we didn't plan for."
cards.body:
> **SAY:** "There's no dragon here. But there's the Dreamer, and it's enormous. Are you sure you want to fight it?"

**DO:** Use the Dreamer's form: a shape made of sleeping bells and dreaming mountains. It is not a monster. Players who attack it are attacking the dream, and treat the attack as striking the lullaby, so Session 26 begins as if Maudrin had struck. If the Seventh is not struck, the attack does nothing.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 19: "A player wants to leave, a character dies, or a player is absent."
cards.body: **DO:** Follow your table's agreed rules. If a character dies, give the player a new character who arrives in Pellmoor or Hallowmere with a hook from Part 7.7. If a player is absent, play their character as a loyal NPC companion who wants the best for the party, and let them return with one Toll or one Bargain gained.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 20: "We're confused. We don't know where to go next."
cards.body:
> **SAY:** "Let's look at what you know. You have a tongue. You know the Court wants it. You know Ila's father is dead. Who do you trust most, and where do you want to go?"

**DO:** Use the Clue Ladder. Give three clues toward the next location. If players are still stuck after the third, have an NPC approach them with a direct request: Mother Sallow, Captain Rook, Thane Kessa, Corin Aldeth, or Lysse Carrow.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: SITUATION 21: "We want to get the Calla Tongue, but we don't want to go back to Hallowmere."
cards.body:
**DO:** The Calla Tongue is only in the Court's vault, in Hallowmere. If the party did not take it in Session 5, they must return to the city for it, which is a clear choice with a cost. Remind them that the Tithe Clock is running. Give them one NPC who can help from outside the city: Wren Caddock's Bellwright route, or Bet Ostrow, who knows which carts leave the city without a search.

---

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 5.2 Characters
cards.body: *Each entry lists: Role, Look, Voice, Wants, Secret, Stat-lite (see Appendix A), and How They React.*

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 1. ILA HARROW
cards.body:
- **Role:** A 14-year-old girl in Pellmoor. Hears Ossa's Tongue humming. Sees the Drowned.
- **Look:** Thin, grey-eyed, wears her father's ferry coat, several sizes too big. Her shadow falls at a slight angle. Her mother, Nessa Harrow, left Pellmoor when Ila was four, and lives at Kell's Crossing.
- **Voice:** Blunt. Asks direct questions. Counts things when nervous.
- **Wants:** To know why her father drowned. To keep the tongue safe. To be taken seriously.
- **Secret:** Her father did not drown by accident. He had hidden the tongue for twenty years and brought it back to the Mere because the Drowned Choir asked him to. The Court has taken his memory of the reason.
- **Stat-lite:** Commoner (CR 0). Can hear the Drowned. Advantage on Perception checks near water.
- **How She Reacts:** Trusts people who tell her the truth about hard things. Distrusts anyone who says "don't worry about it."

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 2. MOTHER SALLOW
cards.body:
- **Role:** Reed-witch and memory-keeper of Pellmoor. Keeps the ferry ledger.
- **Look:** Small, wiry, in her seventies. Hands stained green from reed-dye. A pipe she never lights.
- **Voice:** Wry, short sentences, sarcastic about authority. Speaks in proverbs she half-invents.
- **Wants:** Her husband's memory returned to her. The village protected.
- **Secret:** Thirty years ago she sold her husband's memory of their wedding day to the Tithe. Since then she has been slowly losing the fact that he existed. She still keeps his stone on the Mere Memory Shore, and she cannot say why.
- **Her husband:** **Davin Sallow**, a net-maker, drowned in the Mere in a storm 30 years ago. His name is carved on the Mere Memory Shore.
- **Stat-lite:** Mage (CR 2), reed-healing as a druid-style spell list. Can read the ledger.
- **How She Reacts:** Respects blunt honesty. Dislikes charm. Will help anyone who brings her a dead person's name to speak.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 3. BROTHER ELD MARROWBY
cards.body:
- **Role:** Ninefold friar running Pellmoor's chapel. Collects the village's Tithes and keeps the reports.
- **Look:** Tall, round-shouldered, ink-stained fingers, a sincere face that has been trained to look sad.
- **Voice:** Soft, careful, quotes scripture constantly.
- **Wants:** To do good within the system. To keep his chapel.
- **Secret:** For two years he has reported Bellwright sympathizers to the Hushmen. The names he reports are the children's.
- **Stat-lite:** Priest (CR 1). Can cast *Silence* once per day.
- **How He Reacts:** Pliant under pressure. If confronted with the children's names, he breaks down and offers help, but first he asks for absolution.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 4. CAPTAIN DESSA ROOK
cards.body:
- **Role:** Captain of the Hallowmere Dawn Order. Honest, tired, and under orders she dislikes.
- **Look:** Broad, weathered, wears a dawn-coloured cloak faded to grey.
- **Voice:** Clipped. Military. Says "we" when she means "I."
- **Wants:** To restore the dawn. To keep her men alive.
- **Secret:** She is sure her senior knight, Ser Haldric Mose, is taking Tithes. She has been waiting for proof that will hold up before a court of oaths. She has challenged him to an oath-duel to make it public.
- **Stat-lite:** Veteran (CR 3). A rallying shout restores 1d8 HP to allies once per combat.
- **How She Reacts:** Respects paperwork and proper oaths. Will bend rules for people who protect the innocent.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 5. SER HALDRIC MOSE
cards.body:
- **Role:** Senior knight of the Dawn Order. Keeper of Vaer's Tongue. Secretly a Quiet Court agent.
- **Look:** Handsome, immaculate armour, always polishing something.
- **Voice:** Courteous, smooth. Uses phrases like "for the good of all" and "the dawn will come."
- **Wants:** Promotion. The Court's approval. The Dawn Order's captaincy, which he believes he will win by the Tithe.
- **Secret:** He is Maudrin Vesk's illegitimate son, and he has been told this by no one. He half suspects it.
- **Stat-lite:** Knight (CR 3). A silence-stone shield negates the first spell aimed at him each day.
- **How He Reacts:** Diplomatically dangerous. Offers alliances and betrays them when a better offer comes. If Rook beat him in the duel, he is disgraced, and his knights desert him.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 6. CHANCELLOR MAUDRIN VESK
cards.body:
- **Role:** Quiet Chancellor and Warden of Silence. The main antagonist.
- **Look:** Elegant, white-haired, dressed in dove-grey silk. Her gloves are silence-stone.
- **Voice:** Measured, warm, reasonable. Never raises her voice. Uses people's names constantly.
- **Wants:** To keep the Silence. To protect people from the chaos of memory and bells. To keep the Tuning Key forever.
- **Secret:** She has read Edda Thorne's diary. She knows the Key, not the bells, caused the Quiet Night. She has kept that truth from the Court for thirty-eight years.
- **Stat-lite:** Archmage-style (CR 6). Casts *Silence* and *Counterspell*. Hushmen guard her.
- **How She Reacts:** She offers a bargain before she offers a threat. If the party refuses, she sends Hushmen. If they accept, she still intends to keep the Key.
- **Her bargain:** "Give me the Tongue your friend is carrying, and I will make sure your memories stay exactly where you put them."

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 7. CORIN ALDETH
cards.body:
- **Role:** Bellwright and the main antagonist of Act IV. Believes the world should be woken.
- **Look:** Thin, burn-scarred hands, a leather apron, always listening with one ear turned.
- **Voice:** Passionate, sharp, occasionally poetic. Hums under his breath.
- **Wants:** To ring the Seventh Bell, to wake Oum, and to end the slow unravelling of the world.
- **Secret:** His grandmother Wenna Aldeth rang the first handbell at Vael Tor sixty years ago. Her death drove his family into the Bellwrights, and he has carried her work since he was a boy.
- **Stat-lite:** Bellwright-Mage (CR 5). Can defer a bell's Toll for one hour: the Ringer pays the same Toll when the hour ends, once per day.
- **How He Reacts:** Enthusiastic about anyone who has rung a bell. Furious at anyone who gave a memory to the Tithe without a fight.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 8. THANE ORU KESSA
cards.body:
- **Role:** Leader of the Ironhorn Compact and holder of Thrane's Tongue.
- **Look:** Huge, bearded, braids of bronze wire, a face weathered but open.
- **Voice:** Blunt, humorous, enjoys a wager. Calls everyone "rider," whatever their skill.
- **Wants:** Bronze for his clans. An end to the Court's Tithe-taxes. A weapon against the Quiet Court.
- **Secret:** He is dying of dead-lightning sickness, caught from handling Thrane's Tongue. He has not told his clans.
- **Stat-lite:** Champion (CR 7). The Tongue's lightning strikes back on a critical hit (2d6 lightning).
- **How He Reacts:** Respects strength and honest bargains. Insulted by lies. Hires the party to fight the Court if they prove trustworthy.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 9. LYSSE CARROW
cards.body:
- **Role:** Scholar and keeper of the Bone Archive in Hallowmere. Believes Mirel's Tongue is in the archive. Does not know the Librarian holds it.
- **Look:** Ink-smudged, nervous, hair pinned with a bone pin, a satchel of books that are slightly too heavy.
- **Voice:** Excitable, precise, cites sources constantly, trails off when frightened.
- **Wants:** The truth about the Quiet Night. To read Edda Thorne's diary.
- **Secret:** She has been Tithed twice. Her missing memories are filed in the Bone Archive under other people's names.
- **Stat-lite:** Scholar (CR 1). Has read every catalogued book in the archive, but the Sealed Stacks are not catalogued. Reads ancient bell-script.
- **How She Reacts:** Grateful to anyone who treats her as a person. Frightened by Hushmen.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 10. ONDRA SALLOW (THE CANTOR)
cards.body:
- **Role:** Leader of the Drowned Choir. A ferry-woman who drowned in the Mere in 152 SS, 260 years ago, and has sung there ever since.
- **Look:** A pale, long-haired figure in a wet ferry-coat, skin the colour of river stone, eyes too bright.
- **Voice:** Sings. Speaks only in lines of hymns she improvises.
- **Wants:** To be remembered by name. To be released.
- **Secret:** Mother Sallow is her descendant. Ondra's ledger, which the Court tried to take, is the one Mother Sallow keeps.
- **Stat-lite:** Drowned Singer, Elite (CR 4 in Act II, CR 6 in Act V). Her hymn gives her allies +2 to saves against fear.
- **How She Reacts:** Attacks the forgetful. Speaks with the grieving. Bargains for a true memory of the dead.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 11. THE GLASS SEXTON (IMBER VESK)
cards.body:
- **Role:** Boss of Act III. Former High Sexton of the Ninefold Church. Frozen in a winter-moment since 32 SS.
- **Look:** A glass figure in ceremonial robes, the crown of a Sexton on its head, with the Frost Tongue set in it. Inside the glass, a face that is still very much human.
- **Voice:** Slow, echoing, speaks in long sentences. Still believes he is giving sermons.
- **Wants:** For the world to be quiet forever. To make his confession to someone who will understand.
- **Secret:** He is the only living witness to what the Key did on the Quiet Night. His daughter Cassia took the Key home, and he knows where the family's reliquary is kept.
- **Stat-lite:** Glass Sexton (CR 5). See Appendix A.
- **How He Reacts:** Threatens, then pleads. Will reveal the truth about the Key if the party breaks the winter-moment.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 12. TAM HARROW (DECEASED)
cards.body:
- **Role:** Ila's father, a ferryman who drowned six weeks before the campaign.
- **Look:** Lives in memory only. Survivors describe a broad man with a laugh like a dropped bucket.
- **Voice:** Appears to the party only in a Mere Memory (Part 11.4).
- **Wants:** To return the tongue to the Choir. To keep Ila safe from the Court.
- **Secret:** He stole Ossa's Tongue from the Court's store in 392 SS and hid it in the reeds. Six weeks ago he took it back out to return it to the bell, and he drowned on the way.
- **Stat-lite:** Use Commoner stats, or Drowned Singer if he appears in a Mere Memory.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 13. OLD GARROW (BRASSFALL GHOST-FOREMAN)
cards.body:
- **Role:** A ghost who haunts the Old Works in Brassfall. Found the dead lightning and died in the collapse of 372 SS.
- **Look:** Grey-bearded, carrying a lamp that burns blue. The lamp holds a storm-stone that tethers him to the mine.
- **Voice:** Gruff, impatient, funny. Calls the party "lads and lasses" no matter what they look like.
- **Wants:** His daughter Yenna to know he is sorry. His mine's dead lightning to stay sealed.
- **Secret:** He sealed the shafts too well and the Ironhorn found them anyway. He blames himself for the raid.
- **Stat-lite:** Specter (CR 1). Can lead the party safely through the mines.
- **How He Reacts:** Likes people who work hard and speak plainly. Hates Court inspectors.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 14. YARA THENN
cards.body:
- **Role:** Glassreach scavenger who cuts glass-flowers that hold preserved moments.
- **Look:** Shaved head, fingerless leather gloves, a glass-cutting saw at her hip.
- **Voice:** Sardonic, practical, talks about money constantly, is secretly sentimental.
- **Wants:** Enough coin to leave the north. A map of the Frost Spire.
- **Secret:** She has a glass-flower containing a moment of her dead brother's laugh. She has never opened it, because she is afraid it will shatter.
- **Stat-lite:** Scout (CR 2). Knows every frozen path in Glassreach.
- **How She Reacts:** Sells everything. Trades favours for tools rather than coin.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 15. LADY ISOLDE DRAVE
cards.body:
- **Role:** A noblewoman of Hallowmere who hosts the Court's social events. Sells information.
- **Look:** Silver jewellery, a grey lace mask, always holding a glass of something warm.
- **Voice:** Flirtatious, cutting, tells half-truths beautifully.
- **Wants:** Power inside the Court. Her son's safety.
- **Secret:** She has been selling Tithed memories to the Ironhorn Compact.
- **Stat-lite:** Noble-Spy (CR 2). Three hidden daggers and an excellent memory for other people's secrets.
- **How She Reacts:** Likes clever people. Hates being out-talked. Follows the party north with a Hushman escort if they leave Hallowmere (Session 9).

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 16. JONAH BRAY
cards.body:
- **Role:** A nine-year-old Blank in Hallowmere who has given away his family's memories. He does not know his parents.
- **Look:** Thin, big eyes, always holding a wooden bird he cannot explain.
- **Voice:** Sweet, very literal, repeats what others say.
- **Wants:** To remember his mother's face.
- **Secret:** The wooden bird was carved by his father, Ilam Bray, who is now a Hushman. His mother, Mara Bray, was Tithed of him and is a Blank in Hallowmere.
- **Stat-lite:** Commoner (CR 0).
- **How He Reacts:** Attaches to whoever is kind to him. Frightened of Hushmen.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 17. ILAM BRAY
cards.body:
- **Role:** A Hushman who wears the Court's gloves and does not remember his son's name.
- **Look:** Grey-faced, silence-stone gloves, an old knife with fresh whittling shavings in his pocket.
- **Voice:** Halting. Repeats questions. Apologises often.
- **Wants:** To find his son. To stop being a Hushman.
- **Secret:** He is Jonah's father, and he knows the wooden bird is his. He has never been able to say it.
- **Stat-lite:** Hushman (CR 1/2).
- **How He Reacts:** If reunited with Jonah, he deserts the Hushmen and gives the party a key to the Tithe-Ledger Room's back door (Session 7).

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 18. THE TIDEWARDEN
cards.body:
- **Role:** A hooded ferryman who takes travellers across the Mute Mere for a price paid in memory.
- **Look:** Hooded, an oar that is always dripping, a voice like water over stones.
- **Voice:** Terse. Speaks in riddles, but never lies.
- **Wants:** To carry the dead to rest.
- **Secret:** The dead ferryman on the sandbank in Session 2 is his old body. He left it when he took up Ossa's oar, becoming a bell-spirit of the Mere.
- **Stat-lite:** Specter (CR 1). Rarely fights.
- **How He Reacts:** Honest with those who pay in true memories. Cold to liars.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 19. HUSHMAN TOBIAS QUILL
cards.body:
- **Role:** Quiet Court collector who appears in Pellmoor in Act I.
- **Look:** Pale, grey gloves, a sharp smile, a silence-stone pendant.
- **Voice:** Polite, bureaucratic, always has a form.
- **Wants:** His quota met. A promotion.
- **Secret:** He has been Tithed himself. He does not remember his sister.
- **Stat-lite:** Hushman (CR 1/2). Silence-stone gloves: his strikes make no sound and cannot be detected by Tonework.
- **How He Reacts:** Pushy but not murderous. Takes bribes. Reports anyone who refuses.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 20. WREN CADDOCK
cards.body:
- **Role:** A Quiet Court spy inside the Bellwrights. Feeds the Court names.
- **Look:** Plain, freckled, cheerful, always sewing something.
- **Voice:** Warm, chatty, asks a lot of questions.
- **Wants:** Her daughter's safety. Redemption.
- **Secret:** She has been trying to get out for two years. She has also warned the Bellwrights about several raids, which is why some of them survived.
- **Stat-lite:** Spy (CR 1).
- **How She Reacts:** Wants to be trusted. Breaks if someone is cruel to her.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 21. ANSEL QUAY
cards.body:
- **Role:** Maudrin's steward and archivist. Holds the key to the Tithe-Ledger Room, and knows the routes Maudrin's Hushmen take from the palace to the Tor.
- **Look:** Stooped, ink on his cuffs, wears reading spectacles he does not need.
- **Voice:** Prim, precise, whispers when nervous.
- **Wants:** Maudrin's approval. Enough money to retire to the coast.
- **Secret:** He has been copying the Tithe-Ledger for the Bellwrights. He is more loyal to Wren Caddock than to Maudrin.
- **Stat-lite:** Commoner-clerk (CR 0), with advantage on Sleight of Hand checks around documents.
- **How He Reacts:** Bribable. Reveals the Tithe-Ledger Room's door for a Gift or for a promise of safety.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 22. BET OSTROW
cards.body:
- **Role:** An old baker in Hallowmere who was Tithed of the Last Ringing. Rang Calla's bell as a child.
- **Look:** Small, round, flour on her sleeves, very quick hands.
- **Voice:** Cheerful, sometimes stops mid-sentence and cries without knowing why.
- **Wants:** To know why she cries when bread is broken.
- **Secret:** She still remembers the tune of the harvest-bell in her hands, though not in her head.
- **Stat-lite:** Commoner (CR 0).
- **How She Reacts:** Gives bread to anyone who looks hungry. Freezes at the sound of a bell.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 23. THE LIBRARIAN OF THE SEALED BOOK
cards.body:
- **Role:** An ancient mind living in the Sealed Stacks of the Bone Archive. Speaks through a book with no words.
- **Look:** A book with no words. When opened, it shows each reader their own face.
- **Voice:** Reads aloud from pages that appear as the party speaks.
- **Wants:** To be read. To be understood.
- **Secret:** The Librarian began as Edda Thorne's tuning pages, bound into a book by Court archivists who could not bear to burn them. It has been reading itself ever since. It keeps Mirel's Tongue because the Tongue, like every memory in the archive, belongs to whoever reads it last.
- **Stat-lite:** Use Scholar (CR 1) for talk, Dawn Order Knight (CR 3) if forced into combat.
- **How It Reacts:** Answers one question for each true memory offered. It may trade Mirel's Tongue for a dream the giver has never told anyone.

---

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 24. YENNA GARROW
cards.body:
- **Role:** Old Garrow's daughter, a rider of the Ironhorn Compact. Keeps the horses at the foothills camp.
- **Look:** Sun-darkened, a red horse-skull on her tent, a long bronze braid she has never cut.
- **Voice:** Quiet and gruff like her father, but quicker to smile.
- **Wants:** Her father to rest. The Ironhorn to stop bleeding for Kessa's war.
- **Secret:** She has heard her father's voice in the Old Works for a year, and has never told the Thane.
- **Stat-lite:** Ironhorn Rider (CR 1), with a bow and a lance.
- **How She Reacts:** Respects anyone who carries a debt honestly. Her younger sister is the Storm-Chaser in Part 11.6.

cards.consequence: DM reference; not a recorded event.
cards.source: The Seventh Bell · supplied campaign guide
cards.title: 25. TRISTAN VESK
cards.body:
- **Role:** Maudrin's cousin, and the Court's likely next Chancellor. Waiting in the wings.
- **Look:** Soft-spoken, always in grey, a smile that never reaches the eyes.
- **Voice:** Careful, legalistic, flatters the party's ambitions.
- **Wants:** Maudrin's chair, and the Key, which he believes will make him Warden.
- **Secret:** He has written to the Ninefold Church's council, offering the Court to the Ironhorn if Maudrin falls.
- **Stat-lite:** Noble-Spy (CR 2).
- **How He Reacts:** Makes deals faster than Maudrin does, and breaks them sooner.

---

pages.title: HOW TO USE THIS BOOK
pages.body:
This book is long on purpose. You do not need to memorize it. Read these before your first session:

1. **Part 1, Start Here** (15 minutes). Core ideas, the session-zero script, and a map of your first three sessions.
2. **Part 2, The World** (20 minutes). Just enough to answer players' questions, plus the rules for bells and Tolls.
3. **Part 8, Act I** (30 minutes). This is where your first three sessions happen.

Everything else you can read as you go. The **Glossary** (Part 4) explains any term that confuses you. **Part 9, Handling Player Choices,** covers what to do when players do something this book did not predict, which will happen in the first ten minutes.

**The canon rule:** Part 3.3 (the Canon Sheet) is the single source of truth for dates, family lines, and who is alive. If any two sections disagree, the Canon Sheet wins.

**Reading boxes** look like this:

> **SAY:** *Words to read aloud, or paraphrase, to your players.*

**Do boxes** look like this:

> **DO:** *Something you do with the rules, the map, or the dice.*

**IF THEY…** boxes cover the most likely player decisions. Treat them as flowcharts.

---

pages.title: 1.1 The Three Jobs of a DM
pages.body:
1. **Describe.** Tell the players what they see, hear, smell, and feel. Then stop talking and let them act.
2. **Adjudicate.** When players try something, decide whether it works, what it costs, and how long it takes. Use dice when the outcome is uncertain. Skip them when the outcome is obvious or unimportant.
3. **React.** The world does not wait. Factions move, rumours spread, and NPCs remember what the party did. Something should change in every session.

pages.title: 1.2 The One Rule That Matters Most
pages.body:
**Say "yes," or "yes, but," or "no, and here is what you can do instead."**

Never say "no" and stop. A flat "no" kills momentum. When a player asks for something you did not plan:

- **"Yes"**: it works as described.
- **"Yes, but"**: it works, and it costs something: time, a resource, a favour owed, or a Toll.
- **"No, but"**: it does not work the way they hoped, and here is another door.

pages.title: 1.3 The Core Question of Corvane
pages.body:
Every decision in this campaign returns to one question:

> **What do you want to ring, and what will it cost you?**

Bells restore something that was lost. Ringing always costs a **Toll**, and the Toll is always personal. When in doubt, ask the player what their character is willing to give up.

pages.title: 1.4 Session Zero Script
pages.body:
Run this before the first session. It takes 20 to 30 minutes.

> **SAY:** "Welcome to Corvane. This is a campaign about bells, memory, and the cost of getting back something you lost. Before we start, I want to know three things from each of you."
>
> "First, what kind of game do you want? A mostly story-driven game, a mostly combat-driven game, or a mix?"
>
> "Second, is there anything you do not want in the game? Themes, monsters, or topics that are off-limits for you?"
>
> "Third, how do you want to handle it when something uncomfortable happens at the table? I'm going to use two simple tools. A **Line** is something we never include. A **Veil** is something we can include, but we skip past it without describing it. Either of you can call one out at any time, and we'll change course without asking why."

**DO:** Write down every Line and Veil. Post them where everyone can see them.

> **SAY:** "Good. Now let's build characters who have a reason to be in the same place at the same time. I'm going to hand you a few hooks from the world. Pick the one that makes you curious, and we'll start there."

Point players to **Part 7**, specifically hooks H-01 through H-06, which are the strongest starting hooks.

pages.title: 1.5 Pre-Session Prep Checklist (About 30 Minutes Per Session)
pages.body:
- [ ] Re-read the **Act** you are in and its session list.
- [ ] Write down the three most likely things the party will do next. Read the matching **IF THEY…** boxes.
- [ ] Choose one **faction move**: something a faction does off-screen this week. Write it down.
- [ ] Choose one **rumour** from Part 11 that the party can overhear.
- [ ] Know the names, voices, and one secret of the three NPCs most likely to appear.
- [ ] Check the **Toll Tracker** (Appendix B.1) so you know who has paid what.
- [ ] Check the **Tithe Clock** (Part 2.12) and the **Faction Clock** (Appendix B.3).
- [ ] Decide how you will end the session. End on a question, not a resolution.

pages.title: 1.6 The Five Things Players Remember
pages.body:
Most players remember these five things about any campaign. Make sure all five happen to your players:

1. A moment where they **changed a character's life**, for better or worse.
2. A **bell** they rang, and what it cost.
3. A **person** they helped or betrayed, and whether that person came back.
4. A **place** they saw that they will never forget.
5. A **choice with no clean answer**.
pages.quote:

pages.title: 2.1 The Big Idea
pages.body:
Corvane is a world that was once rung like a great cathedral. Seven bells, each cast from the bones of the first mountains, held the world in shape. Each bell kept one part of life in its proper form: dawn, memory, winter, harvest, storm, dreams, and sleep.

Four hundred and twelve years ago, the bells fell silent in a single night, the **Quiet Night**. The world did not end. It drifted. The dawn turned grey. Winter froze into glass. The dead could not rest. Harvests failed. Nightmares walked the roads.

The people of Corvane have adapted to the silence. They have built a religion around not hearing bells. They trade memories for coin. They have forgotten what the bells sounded like.

Six weeks ago, a ferry-family's net came up from the Mute Mere holding a bronze tongue. It was humming.

pages.title: 2.2 Tone and Feel
pages.body:
**Corvane is melancholy, not hopeless.** It has a quiet beauty. The people are tough, practical, and a little sad. They are good at surviving and bad at trusting authority.

Three touchstones for describing the world:

- **Sound is central.** Describe what things sound like. A place is quiet, humming, cracked, or ringing.
- **Light is wrong.** Dawn is grey in Hallowmere. Winter light in Glassreach never changes. Brassfall's sky flickers without clouds.
- **Memory is currency.** People remember things in the wrong order. Some have blank spots where someone they loved used to be.

pages.title: 2.4 Geography
pages.body:
Corvane is one continent, **Hesk**, bordered by the **Ninefold Shore** to the south and east. The campaign happens in the middle of the continent.

- **The Ninefold Shore:** coastal cities and the ports of the Quiet Court. Hallowmere is the capital.
- **The North Road and Kell's Crossing:** the road from Hallowmere north into the Ninefold hills. Kell's Crossing is a fork where the road meets the old Pellmoor track. Farmland gone to ash.
- **The Mute Mere:** a vast, still lake hiding the drowned town of Old Pellmoor. The living village of **Pellmoor** sits on its western shore.
- **Vael Tor:** a central high hill with the Sleeping Hall and the Hush Shrine. Nightmares are strongest here.
- **Brassfall:** eastern mountains of bronze ore, full of dead lightning.
- **Glassreach:** the northwestern forest where winter froze into glass.
- **The Ironhorn Steppe:** the northern grasslands, held by the Ironhorn Compact, a confederation of horse-clans. Its foothills meet Brassfall.

| Hallowmere | Kell's Crossing | 3 days | North Road. |
| Kell's Crossing | Glassreach | 5 days | Through the Ninefold hills. Glass cuts. |
| Hallowmere | Glassreach | 8 days | North Road, via Kell's Crossing. |
| Glassreach | Brassfall | 6 days | Around the Ironhorn foothills. |
| Vael Tor | Brassfall | 4 days | Along the Thrane Road. |

pages.title: 2.5 The Calendar and the Notation
pages.body:
The current year is **412 SS** (*Since the Silence*). Years are counted from the Quiet Night.

- **SS** means years *since* the Quiet Night. 0 SS is the night itself. 412 SS is now.
- **BS** means years *before* the Quiet Night. 1 BS is the year before the Silence.

Corvane has twelve months, named for the months the bells once marked: *Vaermont, Ossamonth, Hiemeth, Callan, Thranmar, Mirelle, Yshen, Dawnfall, Ashwake, Glassfast, Emberlea, Stillmoor*. You do not need to remember them.

**The days of the week are named for the bells:**

- **Vaerday:** lawful, good for oaths and contracts.
- **Ossday:** mourning. People visit graves.
- **Hiemeday:** cold. Shops close early.
- **Calladay:** market day in most towns. Ash-bread is eaten in memory of the Ash Years.
- **Thranday:** storm-day. Travel is dangerous (even though no storms have come, people still fear them).
- **Mirelday:** dreams. People share visions.
- **Hushday:** unlucky. Nobody starts anything important on Hushday.

pages.title: 2.6 Bell Magic: Tonework
pages.body:
Magic in Corvane is **Tonework**. It draws on the resonance of the bells, even silent ones. Spellcasters feel it as a hum behind their teeth.

**Three rules of Tonework:**

1. **Every spell has a note.** Casters who study Tonework learn to hum, sing, or strike a tone while casting. Inside a silence-stone field, Tonework fails entirely.
2. **Silence is a resource.** The Quiet Court uses silence-stones, grey stones that absorb tone. They are the reason the Court controls magic in its cities. Hushmen wear silence-stone gloves.
3. **Bells never give freely.** Any magic that touches a bell's domain demands a Toll.

**Player options:**

- **Bell-Touched (Background or Feat).** Your character can hear one silent bell. You know its domain and roughly where it hangs. Gain proficiency in one of Insight, Religion, or Performance, and one Tonework cantrip (see the Glossary entry for *Tonework*).
- **Tone-Scholar (Wizard subclass).** Studies the grammar of tones. Can cast *Silence* and *Tongue-Sense*, which detects any bell within 60 feet.
- **Bellwright (Artificer-style).** Builds and repairs bells and Tongues. Can craft a Tongue, at the cost of a Gift (see 2.7).

pages.title: 2.7 The Toll
pages.body:
A **Toll** is the price of ringing a bell. The Ringer pays it, and it is always personal.

**The six Toll types.** Each bell demands the Toll type listed for it in the Ring Table (2.11). The Ringer chooses the specific memory, name, sense, fear, or gift within that type. If the Ringer refuses to choose, the DM chooses within that type.

1. **A Memory.** The Ringer forgets a specific memory, named by the player. The Ringer still knows *that* something happened, but not what it felt like. The player writes the memory on the Toll Tracker.
2. **A Year.** The Ringer ages one year, permanently. Mechanically: -1 to Constitution saving throws until the next long rest. Describe a grey streak in the hair if you like.
3. **A Sense.** The Ringer loses one sense for one full day: sight, hearing, taste, smell, or touch. Disadvantage on checks that depend on that sense.
4. **A Name.** One NPC chosen by the DM forgets the Ringer's name. Use sparingly. It is a good Toll for a Ringer who is already alone.
5. **A Fear.** The Ringer loses one fear, chosen by the player, for one full day. When the day ends, the fear returns. For that one day, the Ringer may walk where they once could not.
6. **A Gift.** The Ringer gives something they value freely to someone in need, and it is never returned. The Court calls this a Tithe with no receipt.

**Rules for Tolls:**

- A Ringer may pay more than one Toll type. The Ringing of Ysh requires all six (see 2.11).
- Tolls accumulate. Players will feel them in Acts IV and V.
- Record every Toll on the Toll Tracker (Appendix B.1).
- Memory losses from the stairs of the Hush and from Mere Memories are not Tolls. They follow the scene's own rule, and the player still records them on the Toll Tracker.
- The Great Toll (Part 10.3) is never one of the six. It is paid only on Path 1, in addition to the six Tolls.

pages.title: 2.8 The Silence's Effects by Region
pages.body:
Each silent bell has an active effect in its region. Use these as scene-setting tools and as consequences.

**Hallowmere (Vaer silent).** The sun rises as a grey disc behind permanent cloud. Shadows are soft. Church bells ring false. *Effect:* dawn-based abilities are weakened. Ordinary people are always tired.

**The Mute Mere (Ossa silent).** The dead's memories bleed into the water. A character who spends a full night on the shore rolls on the Mere Memory table (Part 11.4) unless they make a DC 12 Wisdom save. Drowned bodies do not decay.

**Glassreach (Hieme silent).** Winter froze at one moment, in one place, on the first night of the Long Unraveling. Trees are glass. Animals are caught mid-step. Time passes for living travellers. The Stilled and the frozen trees do not age. *Effect:* a character who spends more than an hour inside Glassreach without a warm cloak takes 1 cold damage per hour after that first hour.

**Brassfall (Thrane silent).** Thrane's storms stopped on the Quiet Night, and no storm has crossed the mountains since. The dead lightning those storms left behind still sleeps in the stone: storm-stones. Pick the wrong one and it discharges. *Effect:* metal weapons spark near storm-stones. Miners must check for discharge.

**Kell's Crossing (Calla silent).** Ash fields. The old harvest-songs are forbidden. People are generous only in secret. *Effect:* food costs double. A character who gives a Gift here gains Inspiration once per session.

**Vael Tor (Mirel silent).** Dreams leak. At night the **Sleepless** walk. The windows of the Sleeping Hall show visions that are not yours. *Effect:* long rests on Vael Tor require a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the character wakes with a nightmare that gives disadvantage on the first Insight check the next day. If they fail by 5 or more, a Sleepless takes shape.

**The Hush (Ysh silent by design).** Beneath Vael Tor, something sleeps. The Hush is a lullaby, and it is cracking. *Effect:* faint humming, and dreams of a vast, slow presence. A character who sits near the Hush Shrine for an hour hears a voice. To some sleepers it is a child singing. To others it is their own voice asking for quiet. It is Ysh's lullaby given a voice.

pages.title: 2.9 Religion: The Ninefold Church
pages.body:
The **Ninefold Church** worships the Silence. Its central teaching is that the bells were a mistake and the world is better in quiet. The Church has nine Quiet Orders.

The Church began as a monastic order of bell-scholars. It became political after the Quiet Night, when its High Sexton, Imber Vesk, was disgraced. The seat of High Sexton has been empty since the Quiet Night, when its holder was disgraced. The Court created the title **Warden of Silence** for its own ruler. It is held today by Chancellor Maudrin Vesk, who also rules the Quiet Court.

The Church is powerful, corrupt, and sincerely believes it protects people from something worse than memory loss. Many of its members are good people who have not looked too closely at the Tithe.

**Key beliefs:**

- The bells caused the Quiet Night, so they must never be rung.
- Memory is a gift to be returned to the Church.
- Quiet is holy.

**The Nine Quiet Orders (name only, for flavour):** the Order of the Hushed Hand, the Mourning Sisters, the Stillwater Brothers, the Order of the Closed Mouth, the Sisters of the Soft Step, the Brothers of the Blind Bell, the Order of the Folded Hands, the Keepers of the Sealed Book, and the Silent Chancel.

pages.title: 2.12 Clocks and Trackers
pages.body:
The campaign uses four simple tracks. Keep them on paper in front of you.

**The Tithe Clock.** Each night of rest inside a Court-controlled city adds one tick, starting from 0. At **6 ticks**, the Court makes a major move: a Hushmen sweep of the city, with a checkpoint on every road. At **12 ticks**, the Court raises the Silence in the city: silence-stones are placed in every street, and magic becomes much harder to cast. Reset the clock when the party leaves a Court city for at least a week.

**The Toll Tracker** (Appendix B.1). Record every Toll, the date, and what was lost.

**The Bargain Log** (Appendix B.2). Record every deal with an NPC and whether it was kept.

**The Faction Clock** (Appendix B.3). Each faction has a clock from 0 to 6, starting at 0. At the end of each session, advance one faction's clock by one. At 6, that faction makes its next move.

pages.title: PART 3: HISTORY OF CORVANE
pages.body: *Players learn pieces of this history through play. The DM should know all of it.*
pages.quote: *Players learn pieces of this history through play. The DM should know all of it.*

pages.title: 3.1 The Timeline
pages.body:
**Before Time.** The **Dreamer**, a god named **Oum**, dreamed the world into being. The dream was slow and vast. To keep the dream from waking too quickly, Oum asked the first mountains to sing. The mountains could not sing, so they gave their bones to be cast as bells.

**3412 BS: Year One of the Choir.** The Seven Bells are cast in the first foundry, at the top of Vael Tor. Each bell receives a domain. Ysh, the Seventh, is given the task of keeping Oum asleep. The other six keep the world in shape while the dream lasts.

**3000 BS to 1 BS: The Age of Chimes.** The bells rang. Ordinary people lived by their tones. Dawns came on time. Harvests came in season. The dead were remembered in Ossa's tone. Historians disagree about whether the Age of Chimes was golden.

**1100 BS: The Founding of the Ninefold Church.** A monastic order of bell-scholars studies the tones. Over centuries it becomes political.

**700 BS: The Bellwright Guilds.** Skilled bell-makers organize. The guilds control the tuning and repair of the bells and build the Bellwright Tower in Hallowmere's hills.

**1 BS: The Last Routine Tuning.** Edda Thorne is Warden of the Bellwright Tower. She tunes the bells under ordinary rites for the last time. In her private diary she records a "note beneath the note" she hears in Ysh's tone, and she writes that she is afraid of it.

**0 SS: The Quiet Night.** High Sexton **Imber Vesk** enters the Bellwright Tower with the Tuning Key, which he has taken from the Tower's reliquary. He orders Edda to tune the bells into one long, gentle spring, so that no season would ever again bring suffering. Edda refuses. She writes a warning in her diary, and gives him a copy of it in person. He tunes the bells anyway. The Key sings against the bells, and all seven fall silent in one breath. The survivors call it "the sound of a held breath." On the same night, Brassfall's storms stop.

**1 SS: The Long Dusk Begins.** The dawn does not come to Hallowmere. The Ninefold Church reorganizes as the **Quiet Court**, a government with a religious mandate. The Court introduces the **Tithe of Memory**: citizens may give up memories in exchange for protection and tax relief. The Tithe funds silence-stones and the Court's control of Tonework. The Court's first Tithe-clerks take Edda Thorne into custody and confiscate her diary. She dies in custody in 9 SS. Her diary is sealed in the Tithe-Ledger Room, in the Court's vault.

**2 SS: Glassreach Freezes.** On the first night of the Long Unraveling, winter stops in one place. Trees turn to glass in the space of an hour.

**2 to 42 SS: The Long Unraveling.** The Court's grip spreads as the Silence spreads. Brassfall's shafts flood with dead lightning and its mines empty. The Mute Mere rises in 14 SS and swallows the old town of Pellmoor. The ferry-folk move to the western shore and keep the name. The first Sleepless walk down from Vael Tor in 20 SS. Kell's Crossing's harvests fail in the **Ash Years** (32 to 42 SS).

**32 SS: The Stilling.** Imber Vesk, disgraced, goes into Glassreach as a penitent. He walks into a winter-moment and does not come out. He becomes the **Glass Sexton**, and he is still there.

**62 SS: The Ironhorn Compact.** Thane Aun Kessa, the first of the name, unites the horse-clans of the northern steppe. The Compact swears never to let the Quiet Court march north.

**112 SS: The Bellwrights Are Banned.** The Court outlaws bell-making and tuning. The Bellwrights go underground. They copy the surviving tuning pages from Edda Thorne's diary and keep the copy as *Edda Thorne's Notes*.

**152 SS: The Drowned Choir Forms.** **Ondra Sallow**, a ferry-woman and keeper of Pellmoor's ledger, refuses the Court's order to hand over the names of the drowned. Hushmen drown her in the Mere. Her voice remains, singing grief in the Mere, and the Drowned Choir forms around it. She is the ancestor of Mother Sallow.

**292 SS: The Chapel to Quiet Rest.** The ferry-folk, who never left the western shore, build the chapel and bell-tower, dedicated "to quiet rest."

**340 SS: The Last Ringing.** At Kell's Crossing, a nine-year-old girl, **Bet Ostrow**, rings the small harvest-bell at the Old Granary against the Court's orders. For one season the harvest comes back. The Court finds her and Tithes her memory of the bell. Bet is now about eighty years old and runs a bakery in Hallowmere. She cannot remember why she cries when she smells bread being broken.

**352 SS: The Great Nightmare Wave.** **Wenna Aldeth**, a Bellwright, rings a small handbell at the foot of Vael Tor. The sound lasts one breath. The Sleepless pour out and kill forty people. The Court blames the Bellwrights, and Wenna is caught and dies in the hunt. She is the grandmother of Corin Aldeth.

**372 SS: The Collapse of the Old Works.** The foreman **Old Garrow** discovers the dead lightning in Brassfall, seals its shafts with his own hands, and then dies in the collapse that follows. His ghost still walks the old mine.

**374 SS: Maudrin Takes the Key.** Maudrin Vesk, twenty years old, takes the Tuning Key from the Vesk family reliquary, where it has been kept since Imber's daughter Cassia brought it home. Maudrin has not stopped listening to it since.

**382 SS: The Ironhorn Raid and Ilse Vesk.** The Ironhorn raid Brassfall for bronze and find Old Garrow's sealed shafts. In the chaos that follows, **Ilse Vesk**, Maudrin's grandmother, seizes control of the Quiet Court and names herself its first Warden of Silence.

**392 SS: Tam Harrow Hides the Tongue.** **Tam Harrow**, a ferryman, steals Ossa's Tongue from the Court's store during a Tithe raid on Pellmoor. He wraps it in oilskin and sinks it in the reed-beds off the ferry-dock, to hide it from the Court.

**398 SS: Ila Harrow Is Born.** In Pellmoor, Tam and his wife have a daughter. Mother Sallow says she is "a listener" the moment she sees the child's shadow fall at the wrong angle.

**411 SS: The Quiet Court's Tithe Ledger Ends Its First Volume.** A quiet year. The first volume of the Court's Tithe Ledger closes. Few people noticed.

**412 SS: Now.**

- **Six weeks ago**, the Mute Mere's ice cracked early. Tam Harrow's net came up with the oilskin in it. The tongue was humming.
- **Two days later**, Tam was found drowned, his face at peace, his net empty.
- **Ila Harrow** has heard the humming every night since.
- The campaign begins.

pages.title: 3.2 Why It Matters
pages.body:
- The bells were not mistakes. They held the world in shape.
- The Quiet Court was founded on a lie. The bells did not cause the Silence. Imber Vesk's attempt to *tune the Seventh Bell's lullaby* caused it.
- Oum is still dreaming. Ysh is still singing the lullaby, but the lullaby is failing.
- No living person remembers the bells ringing. A few people, like Bet Ostrow and Corin Aldeth, carry stories and fragments of them. Most of those people have been Tithed of those stories.

pages.body:

| The current year | 412 SS |
| The Quiet Night | 0 SS |
| The Quiet Court's founding and the Tithe of Memory | 1 SS |
| Glassreach freezes | 2 SS, a single event |
| Imber Vesk, the Glass Sexton | High Sexton at the Quiet Night. Disgraced immediately. Stilled in 32 SS. Frozen for 380 years. |
| Edda Thorne | Warden of the Bellwright Tower. Warned Imber on the Quiet Night. Died in custody in 9 SS. Her diary is in the Court's vault. The Bellwrights' copy is *Edda Thorne's Notes*. |
| The Tuning Key | Stolen from the Bellwright Tower on the Quiet Night. Passed to Cassia Vesk (Imber's daughter). Kept in the Vesk reliquary. Taken by Maudrin in 374 SS. |
| Maudrin Vesk | Quiet Chancellor and Warden of Silence. Age about 58. Descended from Cassia Vesk through Ilse Vesk. Took the Key at twenty. Ilse was her grandmother. |
| Ondra Sallow (the Cantor) | Ferry-woman, ledger-keeper, drowned in 152 SS. Mother Sallow's ancestor (her great-great-great-grandmother). Not Sallow's sister. |
| Mother Sallow | Keeper of the Pellmoor ledger. Age about 75. Her husband, **Davin Sallow**, died about 30 years ago. Their names are on the Mere Memory Shore. |
| Ila Harrow | Born 398 SS. Age 14. Daughter of Tam Harrow. |
| Tam Harrow | Ferryman. Stole Ossa's Tongue in 392 SS. Drowned in 412 SS, six weeks before the campaign. |
| Wenna Aldeth | Bellwright. Rang the handbell at Vael Tor in 352 SS. Died in the hunt that followed. Corin Aldeth's grandmother. |
| Corin Aldeth | Bellwright. Age about 40. His family has tried to finish Wenna's work for three generations: his grandmother Wenna, his mother, and now him. |
| Old Garrow | Brassfall foreman. Found the dead lightning and sealed the shafts. Died in the collapse of 372 SS. His ghost walks the Old Works. His daughter, **Yenna Garrow**, is alive and rides with the Ironhorn. |
| Bet Ostrow | Rang Calla's bell at nine (340 SS). Tithed. Age about 80. Runs a bakery in Hallowmere. |
| Thane Oru Kessa | Thane of the Ironhorn Compact. Holds Thrane's Tongue. Dying of dead-lightning sickness. |
| Ser Haldric Mose | Senior knight of the Dawn Order. Holds Vaer's Tongue. Secretly a Quiet Court agent and Maudrin's son. |
| Captain Dessa Rook | Captain of the Hallowmere Dawn Order. Honest, tired. Her senior knight is Haldric Mose. |
| The Librarian of the Sealed Book | Keeps Mirel's Tongue in the Bone Archive's Sealed Stacks. Speaks through a book with no words. |
| Ansel Quay | Maudrin's steward and archivist. Has the key to the Tithe-Ledger Room. |
| Ilam Bray | Hushman. Father of Jonah Bray. Carved the wooden bird. |

pages.title: PART 4: GLOSSARY
pages.body:
*Alphabetical. Terms in* italics *have their own entry.*

**Ash Years.** The famine of Kell's Crossing, 32 to 42 SS. Survivors eat ash-bread on Calladay as a memorial.

**Bell-Touched.** A person who can hear a silent bell. Usually born that way. Quiet Court agents hunt them.

**Bellwright.** A craftsman who makes, repairs, or tunes bells and Tongues. Illegal since 112 SS.

**Bellwrights, the.** The underground network of Bellwrights. They want the bells rung. Their symbol is a small cup with a crack in it.

**Bet Ostrow.** The girl who rang Calla's bell in 340 SS. Now an old baker in Hallowmere.

**Blanks.** People who have given away so many memories that they cannot recognize their own families. Common in Hallowmere.

**Brass Road.** The old trade road from Brassfall to the steppe, partly collapsed since the Long Unraveling.

**BS.** Years *before* the Quiet Night. See *SS*.

**Canon Sheet.** The table in Part 3.3 that overrides every other date and relationship in the book.

**Cantor, the.** Ondra Sallow, leader of the Drowned Choir.

**Choir, the.** The seven bells taken together. "The Choir is silent" means all seven are silent.

**Clue Ladder.** Three clues per location, in order, with the third naming the place outright (Part 9.1).

**Concord.** The state in which all six bells other than Ysh are rung before the Key is struck or held, creating a chord that restores the world. See Part 10, Path 1.

**Dawn Order.** The knights of Hallowmere, who keep the city's watch. They revere Vaer and resent the Quiet Court's control of the city.

**Dreamer, the (Oum).** The god dreaming the world. Oum has never been seen. Some believe Oum is dying. Others believe Oum is waking.

**Drowned Choir.** The restless singers of the Mute Mere. They sing grief in the voice of Ondra Sallow.

**Edda Thorne's Notes.** The Bellwrights' copy of the tuning pages from Edda Thorne's diary. The diary itself is in the Court's vault.

**Ferry-folk.** The people of Pellmoor. Practical, suspicious of outsiders, careful record-keepers.

**Gift.** A Toll type. The Ringer gives something of value to someone in need. It is never returned.

**Glass Sexton.** Imber Vesk, frozen in a winter-moment in Glassreach since 32 SS. The Silence's first penitent and its strongest servant.

**Glassreach.** The frozen northwestern forest.

**Great Toll.** The Concord's Toll, paid only on Path 1, in addition to the six Toll types. The Ringer gives their name entirely (Part 10.3).

**Hush, the.** (1) The silence that holds Oum asleep. (2) The Hush Shrine at Vael Tor. (3) An insult, meaning "shut up."

**Hushday.** The unlucky day of the week. Ysh's day.

**Hushmen.** Quiet Court agents who collect Tithes and enforce the Silence. They wear silence-stone gloves.

**Ironhorn Compact.** A confederation of horse-clans on the northern steppe, led by a Thane.

**Lightning, dead.** The charge left in storm-stones after Thrane fell silent. Dangerous to miners and to metal.

**Long Dusk.** The grey, endless twilight over Hallowmere since 1 SS.

**Mere Memory.** A memory that bleeds into a character who spends a night on the Mute Mere's shore. See Part 11.4.

**Mute Mere.** The great still lake of central Corvane. It hides Old Pellmoor.

**Ninefold Church.** The religion of the Silence. Now a sub-faction of the Quiet Court.

**Oum.** See *Dreamer*.

**Quiet Court.** The government of the Ninefold Shore. Controls the Tithe, the silence-stones, and the Court's archives.

**Quiet Night.** The night of 0 SS, when the bells fell silent.

**Ringer.** A person who rings a bell. Pays the *Toll*. See Part 2.11.

**Silence Warrant.** A Court order that lets any Hushman arrest the Ringer on sight in a Court city. Issued after Vaer rings (Part 2.11).

**Silence-stone.** A grey stone that absorbs tone. The Court uses it to suppress Tonework.

**Sleepless.** Nightmare creatures that walk from Vael Tor. They take the shape of a sleeper's greatest fear.

**SS.** Years *since* the Quiet Night. 412 SS is the present.

**Stilled.** People frozen in Glassreach's winter-moments. They are alive but cannot move while the glass holds them.

**Storm-stone.** A Brassfall stone holding dead lightning. Handle with care.

**Tam Harrow.** Ila's father. The ferryman who stole Ossa's Tongue and hid it in the reeds.

**Tithe Clock.** The Court's tracker of long rests in its cities. See Part 2.12.

**Tithe of Memory.** The Quiet Court's system of trading memories for protection and taxes.

**Toll.** The personal price of ringing a bell. Six types. See Part 2.7.

**Tonework.** The magic of tones. Cantrips for Bell-Touched characters: *Hum* (a tone that steadies one ally's concentration), *Toll-Ear* (hear the nearest silent bell within 60 feet), and *Muffle* (dampen one sound within 10 feet). Spell notes are sung, hummed, or struck.

**Tongue.** The clapper of a bell. Each bell needs its own Tongue.

**Tuning Key.** The Tongue of the Seventh Bell, Ysh. Held by Chancellor Maudrin Vesk. The most important object in the campaign.

**Vael Tor.** The central hill with the Sleeping Hall and the Hush Shrine.

**Vaer's Belfry.** The tower in Hallowmere that holds Vaer. Now a prison and watchtower.

**Warden of Silence.** The Court's title for its ruler, held by Maudrin Vesk. It was created by Ilse Vesk in 382 SS.

**Winter-moment.** A frozen instant in Glassreach. The Stilled live inside them.

**Yenna Garrow.** Old Garrow's daughter. A rider of the Ironhorn Compact.
---

pages.title: THE QUIET COURT
pages.body:
- **Wants:** Silence, order, and control of the Tithe. The Court believes the bells must never be rung again.
- **Fears:** A ringing bell. A Blank who remembers. A second Vesk with a claim to the Key.
- **Methods:** Tithe collections, silence-stone checkpoints, Hushmen patrols, and bribery of local officials.
- **Ideal:** *Order.*
- **Secret:** Maudrin Vesk alone knows the bells did not cause the Quiet Night. Imber Vesk's use of the Tuning Key did. Maudrin Vesk has read Edda Thorne's diary, and she has kept the truth sealed for thirty-eight years.
- **How They React:** Politely, then ruthlessly. The Court offers rewards before it offers threats, and it will try to buy the party first.

pages.body:
- **Wants:** Bronze for war. Protection for the horse-clans. An end to the Court's Tithe-taxes on the steppe.
- **Fears:** The Court's march north. The dead lightning, which they cannot control.
- **Methods:** Raids, trade, and alliances with other steppe-clans.
- **Ideal:** *Courage.*
- **Secret:** Thane Oru Kessa knows Thrane's bell brings storms. He believes he can aim those storms at the Court. He does not know the bell was cast to hold the weather, not to wage war. His hands are blackening with dead-lightning sickness.
- **How They React:** Directly. They offer trade, then challenge, then alliance, in that order.

pages.title: 5.2 Characters
pages.body: *Each entry lists: Role, Look, Voice, Wants, Secret, Stat-lite (see Appendix A), and How They React.*
pages.quote: *Each entry lists: Role, Look, Voice, Wants, Secret, Stat-lite (see Appendix A), and How They React.*

pages.title: 1. ILA HARROW
pages.body:
- **Role:** A 14-year-old girl in Pellmoor. Hears Ossa's Tongue humming. Sees the Drowned.
- **Look:** Thin, grey-eyed, wears her father's ferry coat, several sizes too big. Her shadow falls at a slight angle. Her mother, Nessa Harrow, left Pellmoor when Ila was four, and lives at Kell's Crossing.
- **Voice:** Blunt. Asks direct questions. Counts things when nervous.
- **Wants:** To know why her father drowned. To keep the tongue safe. To be taken seriously.
- **Secret:** Her father did not drown by accident. He had hidden the tongue for twenty years and brought it back to the Mere because the Drowned Choir asked him to. The Court has taken his memory of the reason.
- **Stat-lite:** Commoner (CR 0). Can hear the Drowned. Advantage on Perception checks near water.
- **How She Reacts:** Trusts people who tell her the truth about hard things. Distrusts anyone who says "don't worry about it."

pages.title: 2. MOTHER SALLOW
pages.body:
- **Role:** Reed-witch and memory-keeper of Pellmoor. Keeps the ferry ledger.
- **Look:** Small, wiry, in her seventies. Hands stained green from reed-dye. A pipe she never lights.
- **Voice:** Wry, short sentences, sarcastic about authority. Speaks in proverbs she half-invents.
- **Wants:** Her husband's memory returned to her. The village protected.
- **Secret:** Thirty years ago she sold her husband's memory of their wedding day to the Tithe. Since then she has been slowly losing the fact that he existed. She still keeps his stone on the Mere Memory Shore, and she cannot say why.
- **Her husband:** **Davin Sallow**, a net-maker, drowned in the Mere in a storm 30 years ago. His name is carved on the Mere Memory Shore.
- **Stat-lite:** Mage (CR 2), reed-healing as a druid-style spell list. Can read the ledger.
- **How She Reacts:** Respects blunt honesty. Dislikes charm. Will help anyone who brings her a dead person's name to speak.

pages.title: 5. SER HALDRIC MOSE
pages.body:
- **Role:** Senior knight of the Dawn Order. Keeper of Vaer's Tongue. Secretly a Quiet Court agent.
- **Look:** Handsome, immaculate armour, always polishing something.
- **Voice:** Courteous, smooth. Uses phrases like "for the good of all" and "the dawn will come."
- **Wants:** Promotion. The Court's approval. The Dawn Order's captaincy, which he believes he will win by the Tithe.
- **Secret:** He is Maudrin Vesk's illegitimate son, and he has been told this by no one. He half suspects it.
- **Stat-lite:** Knight (CR 3). A silence-stone shield negates the first spell aimed at him each day.
- **How He Reacts:** Diplomatically dangerous. Offers alliances and betrays them when a better offer comes. If Rook beat him in the duel, he is disgraced, and his knights desert him.

pages.title: 6. CHANCELLOR MAUDRIN VESK
pages.body:
- **Role:** Quiet Chancellor and Warden of Silence. The main antagonist.
- **Look:** Elegant, white-haired, dressed in dove-grey silk. Her gloves are silence-stone.
- **Voice:** Measured, warm, reasonable. Never raises her voice. Uses people's names constantly.
- **Wants:** To keep the Silence. To protect people from the chaos of memory and bells. To keep the Tuning Key forever.
- **Secret:** She has read Edda Thorne's diary. She knows the Key, not the bells, caused the Quiet Night. She has kept that truth from the Court for thirty-eight years.
- **Stat-lite:** Archmage-style (CR 6). Casts *Silence* and *Counterspell*. Hushmen guard her.
- **How She Reacts:** She offers a bargain before she offers a threat. If the party refuses, she sends Hushmen. If they accept, she still intends to keep the Key.
- **Her bargain:** "Give me the Tongue your friend is carrying, and I will make sure your memories stay exactly where you put them."
pages.quote:
- **Role:** Quiet Chancellor and Warden of Silence. The main antagonist.
- **Look:** Elegant, white-haired, dressed in dove-grey silk. Her gloves are silence-stone.
- **Voice:** Measured, warm, reasonable. Never raises her voice. Uses people's names constantly.
- **Wants:** To keep the Silence. To p

pages.title: 7. CORIN ALDETH
pages.body:
- **Role:** Bellwright and the main antagonist of Act IV. Believes the world should be woken.
- **Look:** Thin, burn-scarred hands, a leather apron, always listening with one ear turned.
- **Voice:** Passionate, sharp, occasionally poetic. Hums under his breath.
- **Wants:** To ring the Seventh Bell, to wake Oum, and to end the slow unravelling of the world.
- **Secret:** His grandmother Wenna Aldeth rang the first handbell at Vael Tor sixty years ago. Her death drove his family into the Bellwrights, and he has carried her work since he was a boy.
- **Stat-lite:** Bellwright-Mage (CR 5). Can defer a bell's Toll for one hour: the Ringer pays the same Toll when the hour ends, once per day.
- **How He Reacts:** Enthusiastic about anyone who has rung a bell. Furious at anyone who gave a memory to the Tithe without a fight.
pages.quote:

- **Look:** Thin, burn-scarred hands, a leather apron, always listening with one ear turned.
- **Voice:** Passionate, sharp, occasionally poetic. Hums under his breath.
- **Wants:** To ring the Seventh Bell

pages.title: 8. THANE ORU KESSA
pages.body:
- **Role:** Leader of the Ironhorn Compact and holder of Thrane's Tongue.
- **Look:** Huge, bearded, braids of bronze wire, a face weathered but open.
- **Voice:** Blunt, humorous, enjoys a wager. Calls everyone "rider," whatever their skill.
- **Wants:** Bronze for his clans. An end to the Court's Tithe-taxes. A weapon against the Quiet Court.
- **Secret:** He is dying of dead-lightning sickness, caught from handling Thrane's Tongue. He has not told his clans.
- **Stat-lite:** Champion (CR 7). The Tongue's lightning strikes back on a critical hit (2d6 lightning).
- **How He Reacts:** Respects strength and honest bargains. Insulted by lies. Hires the party to fight the Court if they prove trustworthy.

pages.title: 9. LYSSE CARROW
pages.body:
- **Role:** Scholar and keeper of the Bone Archive in Hallowmere. Believes Mirel's Tongue is in the archive. Does not know the Librarian holds it.
- **Look:** Ink-smudged, nervous, hair pinned with a bone pin, a satchel of books that are slightly too heavy.
- **Voice:** Excitable, precise, cites sources constantly, trails off when frightened.
- **Wants:** The truth about the Quiet Night. To read Edda Thorne's diary.
- **Secret:** She has been Tithed twice. Her missing memories are filed in the Bone Archive under other people's names.
- **Stat-lite:** Scholar (CR 1). Has read every catalogued book in the archive, but the Sealed Stacks are not catalogued. Reads ancient bell-script.
- **How She Reacts:** Grateful to anyone who treats her as a person. Frightened by Hushmen.

pages.title: 10. ONDRA SALLOW (THE CANTOR)
pages.body:
- **Role:** Leader of the Drowned Choir. A ferry-woman who drowned in the Mere in 152 SS, 260 years ago, and has sung there ever since.
- **Look:** A pale, long-haired figure in a wet ferry-coat, skin the colour of river stone, eyes too bright.
- **Voice:** Sings. Speaks only in lines of hymns she improvises.
- **Wants:** To be remembered by name. To be released.
- **Secret:** Mother Sallow is her descendant. Ondra's ledger, which the Court tried to take, is the one Mother Sallow keeps.
- **Stat-lite:** Drowned Singer, Elite (CR 4 in Act II, CR 6 in Act V). Her hymn gives her allies +2 to saves against fear.
- **How She Reacts:** Attacks the forgetful. Speaks with the grieving. Bargains for a true memory of the dead.

pages.title: 11. THE GLASS SEXTON (IMBER VESK)
pages.body:
- **Role:** Boss of Act III. Former High Sexton of the Ninefold Church. Frozen in a winter-moment since 32 SS.
- **Look:** A glass figure in ceremonial robes, the crown of a Sexton on its head, with the Frost Tongue set in it. Inside the glass, a face that is still very much human.
- **Voice:** Slow, echoing, speaks in long sentences. Still believes he is giving sermons.
- **Wants:** For the world to be quiet forever. To make his confession to someone who will understand.
- **Secret:** He is the only living witness to what the Key did on the Quiet Night. His daughter Cassia took the Key home, and he knows where the family's reliquary is kept.
- **Stat-lite:** Glass Sexton (CR 5). See Appendix A.
- **How He Reacts:** Threatens, then pleads. Will reveal the truth about the Key if the party breaks the winter-moment.

pages.title: 12. TAM HARROW (DECEASED)
pages.body:
- **Role:** Ila's father, a ferryman who drowned six weeks before the campaign.
- **Look:** Lives in memory only. Survivors describe a broad man with a laugh like a dropped bucket.
- **Voice:** Appears to the party only in a Mere Memory (Part 11.4).
- **Wants:** To return the tongue to the Choir. To keep Ila safe from the Court.
- **Secret:** He stole Ossa's Tongue from the Court's store in 392 SS and hid it in the reeds. Six weeks ago he took it back out to return it to the bell, and he drowned on the way.
- **Stat-lite:** Use Commoner stats, or Drowned Singer if he appears in a Mere Memory.

pages.title: 13. OLD GARROW (BRASSFALL GHOST-FOREMAN)
pages.body:
- **Role:** A ghost who haunts the Old Works in Brassfall. Found the dead lightning and died in the collapse of 372 SS.
- **Look:** Grey-bearded, carrying a lamp that burns blue. The lamp holds a storm-stone that tethers him to the mine.
- **Voice:** Gruff, impatient, funny. Calls the party "lads and lasses" no matter what they look like.
- **Wants:** His daughter Yenna to know he is sorry. His mine's dead lightning to stay sealed.
- **Secret:** He sealed the shafts too well and the Ironhorn found them anyway. He blames himself for the raid.
- **Stat-lite:** Specter (CR 1). Can lead the party safely through the mines.
- **How He Reacts:** Likes people who work hard and speak plainly. Hates Court inspectors.
