pages.title: 14. YARA THENN
pages.body:
- **Role:** Glassreach scavenger who cuts glass-flowers that hold preserved moments.
- **Look:** Shaved head, fingerless leather gloves, a glass-cutting saw at her hip.
- **Voice:** Sardonic, practical, talks about money constantly, is secretly sentimental.
- **Wants:** Enough coin to leave the north. A map of the Frost Spire.
- **Secret:** She has a glass-flower containing a moment of her dead brother's laugh. She has never opened it, because she is afraid it will shatter.
- **Stat-lite:** Scout (CR 2). Knows every frozen path in Glassreach.
- **How She Reacts:** Sells everything. Trades favours for tools rather than coin.

pages.title: 15. LADY ISOLDE DRAVE
pages.body:
- **Role:** A noblewoman of Hallowmere who hosts the Court's social events. Sells information.
- **Look:** Silver jewellery, a grey lace mask, always holding a glass of something warm.
- **Voice:** Flirtatious, cutting, tells half-truths beautifully.
- **Wants:** Power inside the Court. Her son's safety.
- **Secret:** She has been selling Tithed memories to the Ironhorn Compact.
- **Stat-lite:** Noble-Spy (CR 2). Three hidden daggers and an excellent memory for other people's secrets.
- **How She Reacts:** Likes clever people. Hates being out-talked. Follows the party north with a Hushman escort if they leave Hallowmere (Session 9).

pages.title: 16. JONAH BRAY
pages.body:
- **Role:** A nine-year-old Blank in Hallowmere who has given away his family's memories. He does not know his parents.
- **Look:** Thin, big eyes, always holding a wooden bird he cannot explain.
- **Voice:** Sweet, very literal, repeats what others say.
- **Wants:** To remember his mother's face.
- **Secret:** The wooden bird was carved by his father, Ilam Bray, who is now a Hushman. His mother, Mara Bray, was Tithed of him and is a Blank in Hallowmere.
- **Stat-lite:** Commoner (CR 0).
- **How He Reacts:** Attaches to whoever is kind to him. Frightened of Hushmen.

pages.title: 17. ILAM BRAY
pages.body:
- **Role:** A Hushman who wears the Court's gloves and does not remember his son's name.
- **Look:** Grey-faced, silence-stone gloves, an old knife with fresh whittling shavings in his pocket.
- **Voice:** Halting. Repeats questions. Apologises often.
- **Wants:** To find his son. To stop being a Hushman.
- **Secret:** He is Jonah's father, and he knows the wooden bird is his. He has never been able to say it.
- **Stat-lite:** Hushman (CR 1/2).
- **How He Reacts:** If reunited with Jonah, he deserts the Hushmen and gives the party a key to the Tithe-Ledger Room's back door (Session 7).

pages.title: 18. THE TIDEWARDEN
pages.body:
- **Role:** A hooded ferryman who takes travellers across the Mute Mere for a price paid in memory.
- **Look:** Hooded, an oar that is always dripping, a voice like water over stones.
- **Voice:** Terse. Speaks in riddles, but never lies.
- **Wants:** To carry the dead to rest.
- **Secret:** The dead ferryman on the sandbank in Session 2 is his old body. He left it when he took up Ossa's oar, becoming a bell-spirit of the Mere.
- **Stat-lite:** Specter (CR 1). Rarely fights.
- **How He Reacts:** Honest with those who pay in true memories. Cold to liars.

pages.title: 19. HUSHMAN TOBIAS QUILL
pages.body:
- **Role:** Quiet Court collector who appears in Pellmoor in Act I.
- **Look:** Pale, grey gloves, a sharp smile, a silence-stone pendant.
- **Voice:** Polite, bureaucratic, always has a form.
- **Wants:** His quota met. A promotion.
- **Secret:** He has been Tithed himself. He does not remember his sister.
- **Stat-lite:** Hushman (CR 1/2). Silence-stone gloves: his strikes make no sound and cannot be detected by Tonework.
- **How He Reacts:** Pushy but not murderous. Takes bribes. Reports anyone who refuses.

pages.title: 20. WREN CADDOCK
pages.body:
- **Role:** A Quiet Court spy inside the Bellwrights. Feeds the Court names.
- **Look:** Plain, freckled, cheerful, always sewing something.
- **Voice:** Warm, chatty, asks a lot of questions.
- **Wants:** Her daughter's safety. Redemption.
- **Secret:** She has been trying to get out for two years. She has also warned the Bellwrights about several raids, which is why some of them survived.
- **Stat-lite:** Spy (CR 1).
- **How She Reacts:** Wants to be trusted. Breaks if someone is cruel to her.

pages.title: 21. ANSEL QUAY
pages.body:
- **Role:** Maudrin's steward and archivist. Holds the key to the Tithe-Ledger Room, and knows the routes Maudrin's Hushmen take from the palace to the Tor.
- **Look:** Stooped, ink on his cuffs, wears reading spectacles he does not need.
- **Voice:** Prim, precise, whispers when nervous.
- **Wants:** Maudrin's approval. Enough money to retire to the coast.
- **Secret:** He has been copying the Tithe-Ledger for the Bellwrights. He is more loyal to Wren Caddock than to Maudrin.
- **Stat-lite:** Commoner-clerk (CR 0), with advantage on Sleight of Hand checks around documents.
- **How He Reacts:** Bribable. Reveals the Tithe-Ledger Room's door for a Gift or for a promise of safety.

pages.title: 22. BET OSTROW
pages.body:
- **Role:** An old baker in Hallowmere who was Tithed of the Last Ringing. Rang Calla's bell as a child.
- **Look:** Small, round, flour on her sleeves, very quick hands.
- **Voice:** Cheerful, sometimes stops mid-sentence and cries without knowing why.
- **Wants:** To know why she cries when bread is broken.
- **Secret:** She still remembers the tune of the harvest-bell in her hands, though not in her head.
- **Stat-lite:** Commoner (CR 0).
- **How She Reacts:** Gives bread to anyone who looks hungry. Freezes at the sound of a bell.

pages.title: 23. THE LIBRARIAN OF THE SEALED BOOK
pages.body:
- **Role:** An ancient mind living in the Sealed Stacks of the Bone Archive. Speaks through a book with no words.
- **Look:** A book with no words. When opened, it shows each reader their own face.
- **Voice:** Reads aloud from pages that appear as the party speaks.
- **Wants:** To be read. To be understood.
- **Secret:** The Librarian began as Edda Thorne's tuning pages, bound into a book by Court archivists who could not bear to burn them. It has been reading itself ever since. It keeps Mirel's Tongue because the Tongue, like every memory in the archive, belongs to whoever reads it last.
- **Stat-lite:** Use Scholar (CR 1) for talk, Dawn Order Knight (CR 3) if forced into combat.
- **How It Reacts:** Answers one question for each true memory offered. It may trade Mirel's Tongue for a dream the giver has never told anyone.

pages.title: 24. YENNA GARROW
pages.body:
- **Role:** Old Garrow's daughter, a rider of the Ironhorn Compact. Keeps the horses at the foothills camp.
- **Look:** Sun-darkened, a red horse-skull on her tent, a long bronze braid she has never cut.
- **Voice:** Quiet and gruff like her father, but quicker to smile.
- **Wants:** Her father to rest. The Ironhorn to stop bleeding for Kessa's war.
- **Secret:** She has heard her father's voice in the Old Works for a year, and has never told the Thane.
- **Stat-lite:** Ironhorn Rider (CR 1), with a bow and a lance.
- **How She Reacts:** Respects anyone who carries a debt honestly. Her younger sister is the Storm-Chaser in Part 11.6.

pages.title: 25. TRISTAN VESK
pages.body:
- **Role:** Maudrin's cousin, and the Court's likely next Chancellor. Waiting in the wings.
- **Look:** Soft-spoken, always in grey, a smile that never reaches the eyes.
- **Voice:** Careful, legalistic, flatters the party's ambitions.
- **Wants:** Maudrin's chair, and the Key, which he believes will make him Warden.
- **Secret:** He has written to the Ninefold Church's council, offering the Court to the Ironhorn if Maudrin falls.
- **Stat-lite:** Noble-Spy (CR 2).
- **How He Reacts:** Makes deals faster than Maudrin does, and breaks them sooner.

pages.title: PELLMOOR (Village)
pages.body:
- **Read-aloud:**
> **SAY:** "Pellmoor sits on the grey shore of the Mute Mere like a dropped lantern. Reed-thatched houses lean toward the water. The ferry-dock creaks. Nets hang from poles like the sails of drowned ships. The chapel bell, which should ring, is silent. Across the water, the Mere is so still it reflects the sky perfectly, except where something beneath it moves."
- **Population:** About 300, mostly Ferry-folk.
- **Key locations:** the ferry-dock, the chapel (Brother Eld), Mother Sallow's reed-hut, the Harrow house, the net-racks, the ledger-house where the old names are kept, and the Inn of the Shuttered Bell.
- **Dangers:** The Drowned Choir sings at night. Hushmen visit once a week.
- **Secrets:** The chapel's cellar holds a rope that once rang Old Pellmoor's bell, and its end is still tied to something under the water.
- **Atmosphere:** Quiet, careful, mournful. Children do not play near water.

pages.body:
- **Read-aloud:**
> **SAY:** "A low room, a fire that is never too hot, and a cask of ale that tastes faintly of river. The bell above the bar has been wrapped in cloth for longer than anyone can remember."
- **Key NPCs:** Dorra Pell, the innkeeper. She does not like questions but remembers every face.

pages.title: OLD PELLMOOR (Drowned Town, under the Mere)
pages.body:
- **Read-aloud:**
> **SAY:** "Beneath the still water, rooftops appear like the backs of sleeping animals. Streets run down to the bottom. A church spire leans. The water is clear enough to see the outlines of doors. In the deepest part, a bell-tower stands like a finger pointing at the sky, and something is singing."
- **Dangers:** Memory-eels, the Drowned Choir, and drowned houses that collapse.
- **Key locations:** the Ossa Belfry (where the bell hangs), the drowned chapel (the Choir's home), and the ferry-stair.
- **Treasure:** memory-pearls, small glass spheres each holding one preserved sensation.

pages.title: HALLOWMERE (Capital)
pages.body:
- **Read-aloud:**
> **SAY:** "The capital of the Ninefold Shore is built on terraces climbing toward a sky that never fully brightens. Grey lamps burn in the streets all day. The houses are pale stone, and the windows are shuttered. At the centre of the city a bell-tower rises, its doors sealed with iron. The sun is a coin behind cloud. People walk with their heads down."
- **Key locations:** the Quiet Court (a silent white palace), Vaer's Belfry (a prison and watchtower), the Bone Archive, the Hall of Tithes, the Terraces of Grief, the Seaward Market (smuggled goods), and Bet Ostrow's bakery.
- **Factions:** the Quiet Court, the Dawn Order, the Bellwrights (underground), and the Blanks.
- **Dangers:** Hushmen patrols, silence-stone checkpoints, Blanks who lash out, and Tithe-brokers who sell memories.
- **Atmosphere:** Polite, controlled, suspicious.

pages.title: VAER'S BELFRY (Hallowmere)
pages.body:
- **Read-aloud:**
> **SAY:** "Iron doors. A stair that climbs past forty cells, each with a grey-faced prisoner humming to themselves. At the top, a bell as wide as a cart hangs in a frame of black bronze, sealed with silence-stone chains. It is the only thing in Hallowmere that is not grey."
- **Key locations:** the bell itself, the Dawn Order's cells, and the chain-room where the bell is kept under silence-stone chains. Vaer's Tongue is kept in the Dawn Order's armoury, not here.

pages.title: THE BONE ARCHIVE (Hallowmere)
pages.body:
- **Read-aloud:**
> **SAY:** "Shelves climb into the dark like the ribs of a great animal. Every book is bound in bone. Some of the spines are still warm. Somewhere below, a voice is reading softly to itself, a story you can almost follow."
- **Key locations:** the Reading Room, and the Sealed Stacks where the Librarian lives and Mirel's Tongue is kept.

pages.title: THE TITHE-LEDGER ROOM (Quiet Court Vault)
pages.body:
- **Read-aloud:**
> **SAY:** "The vault is sealed with grey stone. Inside, shelves of glass jars hold memories, each one labelled with a name. They hum faintly as you pass, like they are trying to remember the tune they used to belong to. One shelf is labelled HARVEST, WITHHELD. A cloth-wrapped bronze tongue sits on it, warm to the touch."
- **Key locations:** the shelf of jars, Edda Thorne's diary (labelled MIREL, LOST), and Calla's Tongue (HARVEST, WITHHELD).
- **Access:** a DC 15 Thieves' Tools check, or a bribe to Ansel Quay (who has the key). Tonework does not work inside.

pages.title: KELL'S CROSSING
pages.body:
- **Read-aloud:**
> **SAY:** "The road forks at a village built on grey ash. Fields stretch to the horizon, black and cracked. Scarecrows stand in rows, their faces sewn shut. A granary tower rises from the middle of the ash. At its top, a bell-frame holds nothing."
- **Key locations:** the Old Granary (Calla's bell), the ash-bakeries, the Empty Sheaf inn at the crossroads, and the memorial stones for the Ash Years.
- **Dangers:** bandits who think the bells are cursed, ash-storms, and starving villagers.

pages.title: 5.4 Creatures
pages.body:
*Full stat-lite entries are in Appendix A.*

- **Drowned Singer.** Undead of the Mere. Sings grief. Slow, and terrifying in groups.
- **Memory-Eel.** A long grey eel that bites and steals a memory on a hit. Found only in the Mere.
- **Glass-Wolf.** A hungry wolf frozen inside glass. It shatters when it falls, and the shards cut.
- **Stilled Person.** A human frozen in a winter-moment. Wakes and attacks when the glass around it cracks.
- **Storm-stone Golem.** A construct of dead lightning, animated by a shard of storm-stone.
- **Sleepless.** Nightmare creatures. They take the shape of the nearest sleeper's fear.
- **Hushman.** Quiet Court agent. Silence-stone gloves.
- **Ironhorn Rider.** A mounted warrior of the steppe. Fights with bow and lance.
- **Tongue-Hound.** A bronze pack-beast bred by the Bellwrights to warn them of Hushmen. It rings when it bites.
- **Glass Sexton.** A glass-encased former High Sexton. The boss of Act III.

pages.title: PART 6: IDEALS AND THEMES
pages.body: *In D&D, ideals are what a character believes in. In Corvane, every bell has an ideal, every faction has one, and every player is asked to answer one.*

pages.body:
| Bell | Ideal | What it asks |
|---|---|---|
| **Vaer** | *Order* | Is it right to keep rules even when they hurt people? |

| **Mirel** | *Hope* | Is hope a lie that makes suffering bearable? |

pages.title: 6.2 The Four Great Questions
pages.body:
Every faction and every ending answers one of these. Ask them of your players often.

1. **Is memory worth its pain?** The Quiet Court says no. The Bellwrights and the Drowned Choir say yes.
2. **Should the bells be rung again?** Yes: the Bellwrights, the Ironhorn, the Drowned Choir. No: the Quiet Court, the Hush Cult.
3. **Who owns the Tuning Key?** The Court says the Vesk family. The Bellwrights say everyone. The Ironhorn say whoever can take it.
4. **Does Oum deserve to wake?** Nobody knows. That is the point.

pages.title: 6.4 The Tone of Each Bell
pages.body:
When a player rings a bell, describe its tone. The tone tells the player what the bell is about.

- **Vaer:** A clean, bright tone, like a knife through glass. Everyone looks up.
- **Ossa:** A deep, slow tone that ripples the water. People hear their dead.
- **Hieme:** A high, thin tone that frosts the windows. Breath freezes.
- **Calla:** A warm, round tone that smells of bread. People cry without knowing why.
- **Thrane:** A sharp, stuttering tone with lightning behind it.
- **Mirel:** A soft, singing tone that makes people sleepy and hopeful.
- **Ysh:** A tone that is almost not there. You feel it in your teeth, and something behind it sighs.

pages.title: PART 7: HOOKS
pages.body: *Hooks are reasons for characters to get involved. Use them at character creation, in session zero, or when the party stalls. Each lists: Who, Where, Why, and a Complication.*
pages.quote: *Hooks are reasons for characters to get involved. Use them at character creation, in session zero, or when the party stalls. Each lists: Who, Where, Why, and a Complication.*

pages.title: 7.1 Starting Hooks (Use These First)
pages.body:
*Note: H-05 and H-06 are set in Hallowmere and the Ironhorn foothills. If you use either at the start, open in Hallowmere at the Session 4 arrival instead of Pellmoor.*

**H-01: The Humming Tongue.** *Who:* Ila Harrow. *Where:* Pellmoor. *Why:* Ila has the bronze tongue her father hid. It hums at night and she cannot sleep. She asks the party to take it away from her. *Complication:* Hushmen are looking for the tongue and will arrive within two days.

**H-02: The Missing Ferry.** *Who:* Mother Sallow. *Where:* Pellmoor. *Why:* The ferry that crosses the Mere to the eastern marsh has not returned in a week. Mother Sallow offers coin to find it. *Complication:* The ferry is grounded on a sandbank in the Mere, guarded by memory-eels, and its dead ferryman is the Tidewarden's old body.

**H-03: The Tithe Quota.** *Who:* Tobias Quill. *Where:* Pellmoor. *Why:* Quill is three memories short of his quota. He hires the party to convince three villagers to give one each. *Complication:* The three villagers are Bellwright sympathizers, and the party will learn this.

**H-04: The Wooden Bird.** *Who:* Jonah Bray. *Where:* Hallowmere. *Why:* A nine-year-old Blank clutches a wooden bird he cannot explain. Hushmen are sweeping the street, and he is frightened. He asks the party to take him somewhere safe. *Complication:* The bird was carved by his father, who is a Hushman in that same sweep.

**H-05: The Dawn Commission.** *Who:* Captain Dessa Rook. *Where:* Hallowmere. *Why:* Rook needs outsiders to examine the Court's Tithe-Ledger. She cannot trust her own men. *Complication:* Rook's senior knight, Ser Haldric Mose, is compromised, and he will know the party is looking.

**H-06: The Thane's Wager.** *Who:* Thane Oru Kessa. *Where:* The Ironhorn foothills. *Why:* Kessa wants a champion for the steppe contest. The winner earns a hearing before the Ironhorn council about the Quiet Court. *Complication:* The champion must stake their weapon. If they lose the contest, Kessa melts the weapon for bronze.

pages.title: 7.2 Act I Hooks (Pellmoor)
pages.body:
**H-07: The Drowned Bell.** A bell is visible in the Mere on calm nights, and villagers say it rings once a year. *Why:* Someone should see whether it rings this year. *Complication:* Diving to the bell reveals the Drowned Choir and the Cantor.

**H-08: The Ledger Page.** Mother Sallow's ledger is missing a page: the list of children Brother Eld reported to the Hushmen. *Why:* The party finds the page in Eld's desk. *Complication:* One of the children is Ila Harrow, reported two years ago. Her father hid that fact from her.

**H-09: A Stone With Your Name.** A stone on the Mere Memory Shore has a party member's name carved on it. *Why:* The party wonders how. *Complication:* The date is ten years in the future. Mother Sallow says the Mere remembers what has not yet happened. Use it as foreshadowing; nothing else need follow.

**H-10: The Night Visitor.** A hooded figure on the Mere asks the party to carry him across the water. He pays in memories. *Complication:* He is the Tidewarden, and he wants the tongue returned to Ossa's bell.

**H-11: The Sick Net.** Fishermen's nets come up full of memory-eels that bite and steal. *Why:* Fishing has stopped. *Complication:* The eels guard a sunken belfry, and the belfry is Old Pellmoor's Ossa Belfry.

pages.title: 7.3 Act II Hooks (Hallowmere)
pages.body:
**H-12: The Quiet Masque.** Lady Isolde Drave invites the party to a Court masque and hires them to steal a document. *Complication:* The document is a list of everyone the party has met who gave a Tithe. Isolde wants to know who they will betray.

**H-13: The Bone Archive's Bargain.** Lysse Carrow asks the party to find Edda Thorne's diary. She believes it is in the Quiet Court's vault. *Complication:* The diary is in the Tithe-Ledger Room. Lysse gave the Court the location herself, years ago, without remembering it.

**H-14: Blanks in the Street.** A crowd of Blanks gathers outside the Hall of Tithes, asking for their memories back. *Complication:* Hushmen are preparing a sweep. The Blanks will be arrested unless someone takes a side.

**H-15: The Oath-Duel.** Captain Rook publicly challenges Ser Haldric Mose to an oath-duel at the Dawn Steps. *Why:* If Haldric's oath breaks, his corruption is proven. *Complication:* Haldric has already sold his oath, and the Court has bet heavily on his win.

**H-16: Wren's Confession.** Wren Caddock approaches the party in Bet Ostrow's bakery. She says she is a Quiet Court spy and wants out. *Why:* She carries a map of the Tithe-vaults. *Complication:* Wren is also the informant who gave the Court Tam Harrow's name.

**H-16A: The Harvest, Withheld.** On the Tithe-Ledger shelf marked HARVEST, WITHHELD, there is a cloth-wrapped tongue. *Why:* It is Calla's Tongue, and it is the only way to ring the Old Granary. *Complication:* Taking it sets off the Court's vault alarm, and Hushmen will search every cart leaving the city.

**H-16B: The Librarian's Price.** The Librarian of the Sealed Book will trade Mirel's Tongue for a dream the giver has never told anyone. *Why:* Mirel must be rung at Vael Tor. *Complication:* The dream the Librarian wants is one of the party's own, and it will not be returned.

pages.body:

**H-18: The Winter-Moment.** A party member glimpses themselves inside the glass, frozen and older. *Why:* They must find out why. *Complication:* The figure holds the Tuning Key and is smiling. Do not explain it yet.

pages.title: PART 8: THE CAMPAIGN, IN FIVE ACTS
pages.body:
*The campaign has five acts. Each has a goal, a level range, a list of sessions, and a transition. The party can skip, reorder, or invert scenes. When they do, read Part 9.*

**Overall arc:** The party begins by helping Ila with a humming tongue. They discover what the Silence is and who is hiding the truth. They gather the Tongues. They ring the bells they can reach, and then they decide about the Seventh.

**The Concord, in brief:** It is possible only if all six bells other than Ysh have been rung before the Key is struck or held. Calla's and Vaer's bells are reachable early. Ossa's bell is reachable early if the tongue is returned in Session 3, and otherwise through the Tidewarden's ferry. Hieme's bell is in Act III. Thrane's and Mirel's are in Act IV, and Act IV's two branches must both be completed.

pages.title: ACT I: THE HUMMING TONGUE (Levels 1 to 2, Sessions 1 to 3)
pages.body:
**Goal:** Learn the basics. Take possession of the tongue. Discover the Quiet Court's interest. Survive the first night on the Mere.

**Central location:** Pellmoor and the Mute Mere.
pages.quote:
**Goal:** Learn the basics. Take possession of the tongue. Discover the Quiet Court's interest. Survive the first night on the Mere.

**Central location:** Pellmoor and the Mute Mere.

pages.title: Session 1: Arrival at Pellmoor
pages.body:
**SAY (opening):**
> "The fog lifts off the Mute Mere in long grey ribbons, and the village of Pellmoor comes into sight: reed roofs, leaning docks, nets like the sails of drowned ships. The chapel bell is silent. A girl stands on the ferry-dock, staring at the water with her hands folded tight. She does not look up when you arrive. She says, without turning: *'Are you here for the tongue, or for the bell?'*"

**DO:** Let the party respond. Whatever they say, Ila answers with a plain question: "Did you hear it too?"

**Scene 1: Ila on the Dock.**
- Ila has the bronze tongue, wrapped in her father's oilskin.
- She will show it only to someone who asks respectfully.
- **IF THEY ARE RUDE:** Ila turns away. Mother Sallow appears and says sharply: "She's a child. You can be a child too, or you can be useful."
- **IF THEY ARE KIND:** Ila shows them the tongue. It hums when she holds it, and the hum fades when she sets it down.

**SAY (when shown the tongue):**
> "It's warm. Not like a hot pan. Like something alive that's been asleep. When it hums, the water on the far shore ripples in the shape of a bell. I've seen it. Nobody believes me except Mother Sallow, and she only believes me because she's scared."

**Scene 2: Mother Sallow.**
- Mother Sallow invites the party to her reed-hut for tea, bitter and made from river reed.
- She explains: the Mere holds the dead. The tongue belongs to Ossa, the Bone Bell. Her husband's name is carved on a stone on the Mere Memory Shore, and she cannot say why she has no memory of his face.
- She offers a deal: keep the tongue safe for three days, and she will tell them what she knows about the Drowned.
- She teaches the response to the Night Song: a simple Ossa-hymn, sung back to the water, that quiets the Drowned for an hour.

**DO:** Ask each player, "What do you want from Mother Sallow?" Let them ask questions. She answers honestly, but she does not tell everything. She knows the Drowned are her ancestors.

**Scene 3: Hushman Quill Arrives.** On the second evening, Hushman Tobias Quill arrives with one guard to collect the village's memory quota and inspect for "unlicensed bell-work."

> **SAY (Quill):** "Good evening. I'm Tobias Quill, of the Quiet Court's Office of Tithes. I'll be brief, since I'm sure you're busy. Pellmoor is short on its quota this season. Several villagers have declined to give memories. And I'm told someone here has been listening to something they shouldn't. Would any of you know anything about that?"

**IF THEY…**
- **…hand over the tongue:** Quill takes it, thanks them, and leaves. He records their faces in his ledger. The Court now knows the party. Maudrin will mention them in Act II.
- **…lie:** Quill is not a fool. He asks one specific question ("Where did the child's coat go?") and waits. If the party cannot answer, he says, "Then I'll look myself," and searches the village. He finds the tongue unless it has been moved.
- **…attack:** Quill's guards fight. Quill retreats, shouting, "You've made yourselves a Tithe-case!" Ila's house becomes the first place the Hushmen will search.
- **…offer a bribe:** Quill accepts coin. He asks for one favour: "A name." If the party gives him Mother Sallow's, he takes it. If they refuse, he takes the coin and says, "Then I'll remember you were generous."

**Encounter (optional, Quill's Patrol):** Quill and one Hushman. See Appendix A.

**Session 1 end:** The Hushmen raid Ila's house that night, or the party hears the Drowned Choir for the first time. Either way, end on the question: "Who was singing?"
pages.quote:
**SAY (opening):**
> "The fog lifts off the Mute Mere in long grey ribbons, and the village of Pellmoor comes into sight: reed roofs, leaning docks, nets like the sails of drowned ships. The chapel bell is silent. A girl stands on the ferry-dock, staring at the water with her hands folded tight. She

pages.title: Session 2: The Mere at Night
pages.body:
**SAY (night):**
> "The water is perfectly still. Fog lies on it like a sheet. From somewhere beneath the surface, a woman begins to sing. It is not loud. It is grief in a voice you almost recognize. Every word is a name. You hear your own name, then the name of someone you lost, then a name you don't know, and then yours again."

**Scene 1: The Night Song.**
- Everyone in the village hears the song. Villagers hum back to keep the Drowned quiet. This is a ritual.
- Anyone who sings the response (a simple Ossa-hymn, which Mother Sallow teaches) quiets the song for one hour.
- Anyone who stays through the whole night must make a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw, or roll on the Mere Memory table (Part 11.4).

**Scene 2: The Missing Ferry (H-02).**
- The ferry for the eastern marsh has not returned. Mother Sallow asks the party to find it.
- It is grounded on a sandbank in the Mere's centre, reached by boat or by wading. Its ferryman is dead, face peaceful, a dripping oar in his hands. That is the Tidewarden's old body (Part 5.2, #18).
- Memory-eels circle the sandbank. Fight them (Appendix A), or sneak past with a DC 13 Stealth check.

**Encounter: Memory-Eels (2).** Each hit that does damage steals a memory on a failed DC 12 Wisdom save.

**Scene 3: The Cantor (optional, if the party dives).**
- In the deep water, Old Pellmoor's Ossa Belfry stands like a finger. The Drowned wait there, and the Cantor, Ondra Sallow, does not attack unless the party touches the bell.

> **SAY (the Cantor):** "You have come down to the bell. Good. Tell me, who are you grieving? Do not lie to me. The dead can tell."

**IF THEY…**
- **…answer truthfully:** The Cantor sings the name back to them. She teaches a verse of Ossa's hymn. Learning it grants advantage on the next save against a Drowned Singer.
- **…lie:** The Cantor's eyes go dark. The Drowned Choir attacks. **Encounter:** one Drowned Singer. The Cantor sings from the water but does not join the fight at this level.
- **…touch the bell:** The Choir wakes. The party must escape to the surface. The Cantor says: "Then you'll carry it." Each character must make a DC 14 Wisdom save or lose one memory of the Mere.
- **…ask about the tongue:** The Cantor says, "The tongue was taken from us. Ask the ferry-folk what they owe the dead."

**Session 2 end:** End on the question: "Who was on the ferry?" Mother Sallow's ledger is missing a page, which opens Session 3.

pages.title: Session 3: The Ledger and the Choice
pages.body:
**SAY (Mother Sallow):**
> "I've kept this ledger for forty years. Every name the Mere has taken, every name the Court has Tithed. There should be a page between the year of the flood and the year the chapel bell stopped. It's gone. And I know who would take it."

**Scene 1: Brother Eld's Desk.**
- Brother Eld has the page. It lists the children he reported to the Hushmen, and Ila's name is on it.
- The party can find it by searching (DC 14 Investigation), by befriending Eld (Persuasion or Insight), or by threatening him (Intimidation, which he resists).

> **SAY (Brother Eld, when confronted):** "The page is in my desk, Mother. The Court asked me to keep it. I didn't read it, because I didn't want to. But I know what it says. I copied the names onto the Court's forms myself."

**IF THEY…**
- **…take the page:** Eld asks for absolution. He gives the party the name of one child on the list whose family can be warned, and then he leaves Pellmoor.
- **…expose Eld publicly:** The village turns on him. He flees to Hallowmere in shame. He appears at the Assembly in Session 4 as a Court chaplain.
- **…forgive Eld:** He is changed. He becomes an informant in Act II, and he will betray them unless they keep him close.

**Scene 2: Ila's Name.** Ila recognizes her own name on the list and begins to cry. This is where the party learns why her father was afraid.

**Scene 3: What to Do With the Tongue.** By the end of Session 3, the party must decide. The options:

1. **Return it to the Mere.** Ossa's bell can be rung here (Scene 4). The Drowned stop hunting the village, though release still requires the verse. *Consequence:* the Court's collectors stop coming to Pellmoor.
2. **Carry it to Hallowmere,** to the Dawn Order or the Bellwrights. *Consequence:* Act II begins early.
3. **Keep it in Pellmoor.** The Court will come. The party must defend the village. *Consequence:* Act II begins as a siege, and the village changes forever.
4. **Give it to Maudrin Vesk.** Possible if the party is greedy or desperate. *Consequence:* Ila is Tithed. Act II begins with Ila gone, found later as a Blank in Hallowmere.

**Scene 4: Ringing Ossa (optional, if the party returns the tongue).**
- The party must reach the Ossa Belfry under the Mere. The ferry-stair is the only route, and the Drowned Choir guards it. The Ringer must be at the bell with Ossa's Tongue.
- If the tongue has left Pellmoor, the Tidewarden (H-10) ferries the Ringer to the Ossa Belfry once the party holds Ossa's Tongue again, from the Dawn Order armoury or Maudrin's vault.
- **Toll:** A Memory of someone who has died, chosen by the Ringer (see Part 2.11).

> **SAY (when Ossa rings):** "The bell rings from under the water. It is deep and slow and it makes the whole Mere ripple. Every grey face on the shore lifts toward the sound. The Drowned fall silent, and one voice, very old and very clear, speaks a single name. Then the Mere is only water again, and the reeds bend in a breeze that smells of rain."

**Transition to Act II.** Whatever the party chose, a letter arrives from Hallowmere, bearing the Quiet Chancellor's seal:

> **SAY (the letter, read aloud):**
> "To those who carried the Tongue of Ossa from Pellmoor: the Quiet Court extends its gratitude and its invitation. The Chancellor would be honoured by your presence at the Quiet Assembly in Hallowmere, in ten days. You will be safe. You will be remembered. Nothing you carry will be asked of you that you do not wish to give. M. Vesk, Quiet Chancellor, Warden of Silence."

---

pages.body:
**Goal:** Enter Hallowmere. Learn how the Tithe works. Choose allies among the Dawn Order, the Bellwrights, the Court, and the Blanks. Find Edda Thorne's diary. Recover the three Tongues in the city: Vaer's, Calla's, and Mirel's.

**Central location:** Hallowmere, the Bone Archive, and the north road.

pages.title: Session 4: The Grey City
pages.body:
**SAY (arrival):**
> "The road climbs out of the marshes into the city. Above you, the sun is a grey coin behind cloud, and the light is the colour of old pewter. Lamps burn in every street, though it is midday. The gate guards do not look at your faces. They look at your hands, and at the silence-stones on their own gloves. The city is quiet, the way a held breath is quiet."

**Scene 1: The Gate and the Tithe.**
- Every visitor registers at the Gate Office and gives a "courtesy memory": a small, unimportant memory, recorded in the Tithe-Ledger. A player may refuse, but refusal needs a DC 15 Persuasion check or a bribe.
- The clerk is a Blank. He cannot remember why he works at the gate.
- If the party kept Ossa's tongue in Pellmoor, Hushmen have cordoned the marsh road (DC 14 Stealth to pass). If they carried it early, the Gate Clerk already has their names (+2 DC on Persuasion).

> **SAY (the Gate Clerk):** "Name? Purpose? Oh, you're expected at the Assembly. I have no record of that. But the Court's record is never wrong, is it? Just a small memory, then. Your first sweetheart's name, perhaps? Or the taste of your favourite meal. You won't miss it."

**IF THEY…**
- **…give the memory:** The memory is recorded, and the party is in the Tithe-system. Any Hushman can check their record.
- **…refuse:** The clerk calls the Hushmen. The party can run (DC 13 Athletics or Acrobatics) or talk their way out (DC 15 Deception). If they fail, they spend one day in Vaer's Belfry, and the Dawn Order hears of it.

**Scene 2: The Assembly.**
- The Assembly is a masque in the Quiet Court's white palace. Guests wear grey masks.
- Lady Isolde Drave greets the party and asks many questions about the Mere.
- Brother Eld is among the guests, now a Court chaplain. He will not meet the party's eyes unless they have forgiven him (Session 3).
- Chancellor Maudrin Vesk arrives late and speaks to each party member in turn.

> **SAY (Maudrin, first meeting):** "Thank you for coming. I know you've been through a great deal. I know you've been to the Mere, and that you've seen the bell beneath the water. I want you to know that I understand. I have lost things too. Everyone in this room has lost something to the Silence. The question is only what we choose to keep."

**DO:** Let the party react. Maudrin is patient. She waits for a question, answers it truthfully, and leaves out the most important part.

**Scene 3: Maudrin's Bargain.**
- Maudrin offers safe passage, a Court pension, and a Tithe-exemption for one memory of the party's choosing, in exchange for the tongue they carried.
- If they have already given the tongue to the Dawn Order or the Bellwrights, she offers a different bargain: "Then tell me where it is, and you will be rewarded."

**IF THEY…**
- **…accept:** Maudrin is delighted. She gives them the Tithe-exemption, and she has Haldric take the tongue to the Dawn Order's armoury, beside Vaer's Tongue. The party can recover it later by theft or through Rook (Session 6). *Consequence:* The party owes Maudrin one favour, which she will call in during Act IV (Session 23).
- **…refuse:** Her smile does not move. "Then the Assembly will go on without you. Enjoy the city." Hushmen follow the party for the rest of the Act.
- **If the Tongue went back to the Mere:** skip the bargain and run the Assembly without it.
- **If Maudrin already holds the tongue:** she offers the Tithe-exemption for Ila instead.
- **…threaten her:** She laughs. "Oh, you're adorable. Haldric, please see to our guests." Haldric arrives with Dawn Order guards, which surprises the party.
- **…reveal that they have heard of a key that can ring the Seventh (from any source):** Her face goes still for half a second. Then she says, "I have no idea what you mean," and the Assembly ends early. *Consequence:* The party is now the Court's enemy.

**Session 4 end:** End on the question: "Who in this city can you trust?"

pages.title: Session 5: The Bone Archive and the Tithe-Ledger
pages.body:
**SAY (arrival):**
> "The Bone Archive is a cathedral of books, every spine bone-bound. Some still have a faint pulse. The shelves rise into darkness, and somewhere up there a voice is reading softly to itself, a story you can almost follow."

**Scene 1: Lysse Carrow.**
- Lysse is a nervous scholar who has searched for Edda Thorne's diary for years.
- She believes it is in the Quiet Court's vault, the Tithe-Ledger Room.
- She asks the party to find it for her.

> **SAY (Lysse):** "I've read every book in this archive, and I've found exactly one reference to Edda Thorne's notes. It says the note beneath the note is kept where no bell can hear it. The Court's vault is the only place in Hallowmere sealed against sound. I'm sure of it. I just need someone brave enough to go in."

**Scene 2: The Librarian of the Sealed Book.**
- In the Sealed Stacks, the party finds a book with no words. It shows each reader their own face.
- The Librarian answers one question for each true memory offered. The price is a memory the player is willing to give.

> **SAY (the Librarian's first page appears):** "You have asked a question with a memory behind it. Ask me, and I will answer. Edda Thorne's diary is not on any shelf of this archive. It was taken into the Tithe-Ledger Room, and it has been labelled as something else. Ask me the label, and I will tell you it, for one true memory."

- **The answer to the label question:** MIREL, LOST. This is a true clue.
- **The Mirel trade (H-16B):** The Librarian holds Mirel's Tongue. It will give the Tongue for a dream the giver has never told anyone. That dream is then lost to the giver. If the party refuses the dream, the Librarian accepts a Gift (Part 2.7) instead. If they refuse that too, the Tongue can be stolen from the Sealed Stacks (DC 16 Thieves' Tools or Stealth).

**Scene 3: Breaking Into the Vault.**
- The Tithe-Ledger Room is sealed in silence-stone, and Tonework fails inside.
- Entry requires a DC 15 Thieves' Tools check, or a bribe to Ansel Quay (Part 5.2, #21).
- Inside: shelves of memories in glass jars, each labelled with a name. One jar is labelled with the name of a party member and holds their earliest memory, sealed and warm.

> **SAY (inside the vault):** "The jars are cool, and they hum faintly as you pass, like they are trying to remember the tune they used to belong to. One shelf is labelled HARVEST, WITHHELD. On it, a bronze tongue, wrapped in cloth, is warm to the touch."

**The vault's contents:**
- **Edda Thorne's diary,** wrapped in cloth and labelled MIREL, LOST. Read the Quiet Night entry aloud from Part 3.1.
- **Calla's Tongue (H-16A),** on the HARVEST, WITHHELD shelf. Taking it sets off the alarm.
- **The Tithe-Ledger,** the Court's master book, on the reading stand. Taking it sets off the alarm, as Calla's Tongue does. Ansel Quay can sell a copy instead (Part 5.2, #21).
- **Their own jar,** if they search for it. Opening it returns a lost memory, described vividly.

**IF THEY…**
- **…open their own jar:** They recover the memory. *Consequence:* They gain a clue, and the Court knows they opened it.
- **…steal the diary:** Read Edda's entry aloud (box below). *Consequence:* The Court knows the diary has gone.

> **SAY (Edda's diary, read aloud):** "The seventh is not a bell. It is a lullaby with a voice, and the note beneath the note is the sound of something dreaming. Imber came to the Tower tonight with the Key, meaning to tune the seven into one long spring. I told him the Key is the Seventh's tongue, and that the Seventh keeps the dream asleep. He did not hear me. If he strikes the Seventh with it, the dream will wake, or it will crack. God help us, I think he has already struck it."
- **…take Calla's Tongue:** The alarm sounds in three rounds. Hushmen (4) search every cart leaving the city for the next two days. *Consequence:* The party carries Calla's Tongue out of Hallowmere (Session 9).
- **…trigger the alarm without taking anything:** Hushmen arrive in three rounds. Use the Hushmen Line (Encounter Lists).

**Session 5 end:** End on the question: "What did the Court take from the diary?"

pages.title: Session 6: The Oath-Duel
pages.body:
**SAY (Captain Rook):**
> "I don't have time for pleasantries. The Court is rotten, and I'm not allowed to say so, because the men who could say it have been Tithed. So I'm asking you. Will you help me find out what's in the Tithe-Ledger? Not for the Court. For the people who've forgotten their own children."

**Scene 1: Dessa Rook's Commission (H-05).**
- Rook asks the party to bring her a copy of the Tithe-Ledger, or the original.
- She will protect them from Hushmen for one day and provide a Dawn Order escort.
- She is honest, and she is also trying to use them.

**Scene 2: The Oath-Duel (H-15).**
- Rook challenges Ser Haldric Mose to a public oath-duel on the Dawn Steps. The party can witness it.
- The duel is a contest of oaths, not swords. Each knight speaks one oath and then answers three questions from the crowd. The one who breaks an oath, or refuses to answer, loses.
- If Rook wins, Haldric is stripped of his sword and his knights desert him (see Session 23 for the consequence).
- If Haldric wins, the Dawn Order accepts the Court's control of the city.

**Duel procedure.** Each knight speaks two oaths on the steps, in turn. Then the crowd asks each knight three questions, chosen by the DM from this list: "Did you take a coin from the Court?", "Who taught you the oath you just swore?", "Would you break this oath for your sister?", "Where were you on the night the Ledger was copied?", "Who holds the Dawn Order's silence-stone?", "What did the Court pay you for the armoury key?" A knight who refuses or evades a question loses. The party's DC 15 Investigation, made before the questions, lets Rook answer every question cleanly; on failure, each knight faces one question the DM chooses.

**IF THEY…**
- **…support Rook:** She wins the duel if the party presents the Tithe-Ledger in the crowd (DC 15 Investigation to find the right page). *Consequence:* The Dawn Order honours the party, and Rook gives the party the armoury's Tongues: Vaer's, and Ossa's if the Court took it. Haldric becomes an enemy.
- **…support Haldric:** He wins. He takes the Bellwright names the party has learned. *Consequence:* Bellwright contacts are Tithed before the party leaves Hallowmere (Session 9).
- **…stay out of it:** Rook loses. The Dawn Order falls under the Court. Every Stealth check in Hallowmere is at +1 DC from now on.

**Scene 3: Wren's Confession (H-16).**
- Wren Caddock approaches the party in Bet Ostrow's bakery.
- She is a spy, and she is genuinely afraid.

> **SAY (Wren):** "I'm sorry. I have to tell you something you won't like. I've been giving the Court names. Bellwright names, and one from Pellmoor: a ferryman called Tam Harrow. Two years now. I'd stop if I could, but they've got my daughter. I'm not asking you to forgive me. I'm asking you to take her out of the city before they realize what I've done."

**Scene 4: Bet Ostrow (optional).** If the party is kind, Bet gives them bread. She freezes at the sound of a small bell from a child's pocket, and she cannot say why.

**Session 6 end:** End on the question: "Will Rook's oath hold?"

pages.title: Session 7: Blanks in the Street
pages.body:
**SAY (the crowd):**
> "The Hall of Tithes is surrounded. Hundreds of people, grey-faced, holding up old photographs and drawings and wooden toys, shouting names they cannot quite remember. They do not riot. They only stand and ask, over and over, 'Who was she? Who was I?' The Hushmen are forming a line."

**Scene 1: The Blanks (H-14).**
- The party can intervene. The Blanks will follow anyone who promises to help them recover memories.
- The Hushmen arrest anyone who interferes. A DC 16 Persuasion check can calm the crowd, or the party can fight.

**Scene 2: Jonah and Ilam Bray (H-04).**
- A nine-year-old boy in the crowd holds a wooden bird. He does not know his parents.
- A Hushman at the edge of the line, Ilam Bray, sees the bird and stops.

> **SAY (Ilam Bray, if the party is listening):** "That's my carving. I made it for my son. I don't know his name anymore. I've tried. I don't know why I can't remember. Is he in there? In the crowd? Please. I need to see him."

**IF THEY…**
- **…reunite Jonah and Ilam:** Ilam deserts the Hushmen and gives the party a key to the Tithe-Ledger Room's service passage, along with the Hushman roster. *Consequence:* Ilam becomes a recurring ally. He brings Jonah along in Act IV, as a witness.
- **…attack Ilam:** The crowd turns on the party. They are now the villains of the Blanks.
- **…leave Jonah:** Jonah is taken into Court custody as a Blank. He reappears as a hostage in Session 23 (the Strike).

**Encounter (optional, Hushmen Line):** Four Hushmen and one Hushman Sergeant. Use only if the party escalates.

**Session 7 end:** End on the question: "Where did the child's wooden bird come from?"

pages.title: Session 8: The Glass Letter
pages.body:
**SAY (the letter arrives):**
> "A courier arrives on the steps of your inn, breathless, with a letter sealed in blue wax. It is addressed to the party and contains a single sentence in a shaking hand: *'I am still here. Come to Glassreach before the winter takes the last of me. I.V.'*"

**Scene 1: The Letter's Meaning.**
- I.V. is Imber Vesk, the Glass Sexton. The courier is a Glassreach trapper, paid by a Stilled woman's sister at the forest's edge. The Stilled cannot walk, so the trapper carried the letter out of the glass for them.
- The party can trace the courier (DC 15 Investigation), or simply decide to go.

**Scene 2: Maudrin's Last Word.** Before the party leaves, Maudrin sends a final message through Lady Isolde Drave:

> **SAY (Maudrin's message):** "Thank you for your curiosity. It is, after all, why I invited you. When you come back from the north, I will be waiting, and so will the Key. Give my regards to the Glass Sexton. He was once family, and he will not thank you for disturbing him."

**Session 8 end:** End on the question: "What does I.V. want from you?"

pages.title: Session 9: Leaving Hallowmere
pages.body:
**SAY (leaving the city; read after Scene 1 if the party rang Vaer, or at the gate if not):**
> "The North Road runs up out of the city between grey hedges, and the Dawn Order's watchtower falls behind you. Ahead, the land rises toward the Ninefold hills. Somewhere behind, a single bell tolls once, muffled by the cloud, and then falls silent."

**Scene 1: Vaer, if the party has the Tongue.**
- Vaer's Belfry is a prison. The party can ring Vaer only if they hold Vaer's Tongue (from the Dawn Order's armoury, through Rook, or by theft: DC 15 Thieves' Tools, with two Dawn Order guards at the chain-room).
- Ringing Vaer lifts the Long Dusk over Hallowmere for one day. A real dawn.
- **Toll:** A Memory of a dawn you loved (Part 2.11).

> **SAY (when Vaer rings):** "The bell cracks the grey like a knife through glass. For one heartbeat the cloud tears open, and a line of gold falls across the terraces. Every person in the city looks up. Then the cloud closes again, but the light is still there, a little, behind the grey."

**Scene 2: Kell's Crossing, if the party has Calla's Tongue.**
- The North Road passes the fork at Kell's Crossing, three days from Hallowmere. The Old Granary stands in the ash.
- **Toll:** A Gift, something you value, given to someone in need (Part 2.11). Bet Ostrow is a good candidate, if she is in the party's company.

> **SAY (when Calla rings):** "The sound is warm and round, and it smells of baking bread. The ash on the fields stirs. Somewhere a child laughs, and a woman begins to cry without knowing why. For one season, the grain comes up green across the plain."

**Scene 3: The Follow.** Lady Isolde Drave, having failed to keep the party in the city, follows them north with a Hushman escort. *Consequence:* the party is followed to Glassreach, and Isolde arrives in Session 15.

**Scene 4: The Hallowmere Ending.** Before the party leaves, resolve their Act II choices with a quick round of questions:

1. Did they open a memory jar? If so, what was in it?
2. Did they help Captain Rook, or Haldric?
3. Did they reunite Jonah and Ilam, or leave Jonah in Court custody?
4. Did they accept Maudrin's bargain?
5. Did they find Edda Thorne's diary?
6. Did they take Calla's Tongue? Vaer's? Mirel's (from the Librarian)?
7. Did Wren's daughter get out?

Record the answers on a one-page Hallowmere Ledger kept by the DM, and use them to adjust Acts III to V (Part 9). The Faction Clock tracks faction moves only.

**Transition to Act III.** The party heads for Glassreach with whatever they took from Hallowmere: a diary, a Tongue, a jar, a wooden bird, or a Court seal.

---

pages.body:
**Goal:** Reach Glassreach. Survive the frozen forest. Learn the truth about Imber Vesk. Free the Frost Tongue and ring Hieme.

**Central location:** Glassreach.

**Session 9 end:** End on the question: "Which Tongues did you carry out of the city?"

pages.title: Session 10: Into the Glass
pages.body:
**SAY (entering Glassreach):**
> "The trees appear first, like pale columns in the mist. Then you see they are not trees. They are glass. Every branch is frozen. Every leaf hangs motionless in the air, reflecting the light of a sun that does not move. Somewhere in the forest a bird is singing one note over and over. It has been singing for four hundred years."

**DO:** Describe the cold. Without a warm cloak, a character takes 1 cold damage per hour after the first hour (Part 2.8). Yara Thenn appears at the edge of the trees, selling glass-cutting tools.

**Scene 1: Yara's Camp (H-17).**
- Yara sells glass-cutting tools, warm cloaks, and maps.
- She has a secret: a glass-flower holding her brother's laugh. If asked, she says, "That's not for sale."
- If the party befriends her, she gives them a map of safe paths through the glass.

> **SAY (Yara, if befriended):** "I'll tell you where the safe paths are. You tell me why you're going to the Sexton. Nobody goes to the Sexton for a pleasant chat. And if you're going to die, I'd like to know what for, so I can sell the story."

**Scene 2: The Stilled Clearing.**
- A deer, a fox, and a child stand frozen mid-motion in a clearing.
- If the party breaks the glass around the child, she wakes and speaks one true sentence about the Sexton.

> **SAY (the Stilled child, if woken):** "The man in the tower was sad. He sang to us so we wouldn't be afraid. Then he stopped singing, and the winter kept going, and we couldn't move anymore. Is it still winter out there?"

**Session 10 end:** End on the question: "What is the glass hiding?"

pages.title: Session 11: The Stilled
pages.body:
**Scene 1: The Winter-Moment (H-18).**
- A party member sees a glimpse of themselves inside the glass: older, holding the Tuning Key, smiling.
- This is a seed for Act V. Do not explain it yet.

**DO:** Ask the player what their character feels. Write it down. This is the moment you pay off in Act V.

**Scene 2: The Stilled Ambush.**
- If the party damages the glass around a Stilled adult, that adult wakes and attacks. A Stilled child does not attack; she speaks once and freezes again unless the party threatens her.
- Use the Stilled Person stats (Appendix A). They are slow, but very hard to hit through glass.

**Encounter: Stilled Ambush.** Three Stilled and a pack of two Glass-Wolves.

**Session 11 end:** End on the question: "What did you see in the glass?"

pages.title: Session 12: The Sexton's Sermon (H-19)
pages.body:
**SAY (the sermon begins):**
> "A voice rises from the glass and echoes through the frozen trees. It is calm and patient, like a man who has spent four centuries giving the same sermon. *'Quiet is the gift of the Silence. Memory is the burden of the living. Give your burdens up. Be still. Be at rest. There is no shame in forgetting.'*"

**DO:** Let the party respond. The Stilled and a few lost travellers stop speaking and turn toward the voice.

**Scene 1: The Chapel of Winter.**
- The Sexton's chapel is a cathedral of frozen sound: pews of ice, a glass pulpit, and the Sexton's body within it.
- The Sexton does not attack unless the party breaks the glass around him or argues with him (see Session 13, IF THEY argue).

> **SAY (the Sexton, first words):** "Oh, look. Visitors. Children of the Court, I imagine. You carry the stink of memory-ink on your hands. Sit, please. I have waited so long to say something to someone who might understand. Who rules the Court now? I have not heard its name spoken in four centuries."

**Session 12 end:** End on the question: "Will you listen to him?"

pages.title: Session 13: The Sexton's Confession
pages.body:
**Scene 1: The Sexton Talks.** If the party listens, the Sexton tells them the story of the Quiet Night.

- He ordered Edda Thorne to tune the bells into one long spring. She refused and warned him in writing. He tuned them anyway, with the Key.
- He says that the Key sang against the bells, and the bells cracked on the discord.
- He admits he has regretted it for four centuries.
- He does **not** say what the Key truly is. He says: "The Key was never mine to use. I know that now."

**IF THEY…**
- **…listen patiently:** The Sexton gives them the Frost Tongue, which sits in his crown. He asks them to end his winter and take him with them, so that he can finish his sermon elsewhere.
- **…argue:** The Sexton grows angry, and his voice shatters the glass around them. **Encounter:** Glass Sexton, Phase 1.
- **…ask about the Key:** He is silent for a long time. Then: "The Key passed to my daughter, Cassia, when I was disgraced. It stayed in the family's reliquary. Who holds it now? Tell me, and I will tell you what it is."

**Scene 2: Freeing the Sexton.**
- To free him from the winter, the party must break the glass around him. A DC 15 Strength check does it, or a fire or lightning attack that melts the frost. If the glass melts, the winter-moment ends.
- Freed, he is old and frail, and he does not attack. He remembers every sermon he ever gave, and the confession continues. If the party argues without freeing him, he fights from inside the ice in Phase 1 (frost-form).

**Encounter: The Glass Sexton (CR 5).** See Appendix A. He fights in Phase 1 (frost-form) until his HP drops to 40 or less. He then shatters into Phase 2 (broken-form) with 30 HP. When Phase 2 breaks, the Frost Tongue falls from his crown onto the ice, and the Ringer can take it before the glass reforms.

**Session 13 end:** The Sexton says: "Don't ring the Frost Spire without the Tongue. The winter will come back all at once."

pages.title: Session 14: The Frost Spire
pages.body:
**SAY (the Spire):**
> "A spire of ice rises from the centre of the glass forest like a frozen fountain. Inside it, the bell hangs motionless, locked in frost. Every breath you take freezes on the air. The bell is singing, so softly you hear it only in your teeth."

**Scene 1: Climbing the Spire.**
- The Spire is about 200 feet tall. Three DC 14 Athletics checks get you to the top. A failed check is a slip: the climber drops 20 feet (2d6 bludgeoning) and must start that check again.
- Glass-Wolves guard the base. Stilled Persons watch from the ice stairs.

**Scene 2: Ringing Hieme.**
- The Ringer must hold the Frost Tongue and stand at the bell.
- **Toll:** A Memory (Part 2.11).

> **SAY (when Hieme rings):** "The bell rings once. The sound is high and thin and clear, like a single thread of ice pulled across the sky. The frost on the Spire cracks. The glass trees hum. Everywhere in the forest, something begins to move. The winter is going. Not all at once, but slowly, like a tide turning back."

**Consequences:**
- Glassreach begins to thaw. The Stilled wake over several weeks.
- If the Sexton is alive, he weeps, and the thaw reaches him last.
- The Court sends Lady Isolde Drave (Session 15).

**Session 14 end:** End on the question: "What did the Frost Spire cost the thaw?"

pages.title: Session 15: The Thaw and the Court's Envoy
pages.body:
**Scene 1: The Thaw.**
- The Stilled wake confused, angry, or grateful. They need food, shelter, and a way out.
- A party member who helps them earns the Stilled's trust. In Act V, the Stilled can walk to the Tor and stand in the fight.

**Scene 2: Lady Isolde Drave.** Isolde arrives with Hushmen, having followed the party north (Session 9).

> **SAY (Isolde):** "What a lovely thaw. I'm told you have something of ours. The Frost Tongue, let us say. Give it to us, and the Court will forget your little interference. Refuse, and the Court will remember it very precisely."

**IF THEY…**
- **…refuse:** Isolde smiles and leaves. The Court moves against them in Act IV.
- **…give her the Tongue:** She takes it. The Court now holds the Frost Tongue. If the party carried Calla's Tongue, Isolde asks for that too. Maudrin still holds the Key, and her plan accelerates (Act IV).
- **…attack her:** She has silence-stone gloves and two Hushmen. Fight carefully. Isolde retreats after one round.

**Transition to Act IV.** The party must now choose a branch. Brassfall lies to the east and Vael Tor at the centre of the plain, and both bells are required for the Concord.

---

pages.title: ACT IV: THE STORMS AND THE SLEEPERS (Levels 7 to 9, Sessions 16 to 23)
pages.body:
**Goal:** Ring Thrane and Mirel. Recover the Thrane Tongue and the Mirel Tongue, and ring both bells. Confront Corin Aldeth. Learn what the Key is. Prepare for the Tor.

**Structure:** There are two branches. **Brassfall** (Thrane) and **Vael Tor** (Mirel). The party runs whichever branch they reach first in Sessions 16 to 19, headed 16A to 19A or 16B to 19B. The other branch is compressed into Sessions 20 and 21 using the compression rule below. Both are required for the Concord. Session 22 is the truth of the Key. Session 23 is the Strike.

**Compressing a branch.** To run the second branch in two sessions, use only its first scene (the arrival) and its ringing. Skip the middle scenes, but give the party one clue from each skipped scene.

pages.title: Session 16A: The Lightning Shafts
pages.body:
**SAY (arrival):**
> "The mountains are veined with bronze. Old lightning-shafts drop into the earth like the throats of bells. Storm-stones glitter in the walls, pale blue and humming. The sky flickers above you, though there are no clouds. Somewhere below, a stone cracks like a whip."

**Scene 1: Old Garrow (H-20).** The ghost-foreman appears at the entrance to the Old Works, carrying a blue lamp.

> **SAY (Old Garrow):** "Right, lads and lasses, you look like you can carry a lamp. My girl's in the Ironhorn foothills, near the camp, with a red horse-skull on her tent. Yenna's her name. Take the lamp to her. Tell her I'm sorry about the collapse, and tell her I'm proud of her. And don't drop it. It's the only thing down here that hums on purpose."

**IF THEY…**
- **…carry the lamp:** The lamp holds a storm-stone that tethers Garrow. Carrying it lets his ghost rest near his daughter. *Consequence:* Yenna Garrow meets the party (Session 17).
- **…refuse:** Garrow grows angry and causes a shaft to collapse. Anyone in the passage takes 3d6 bludgeoning damage (DC 13 Dexterity for half).
- **…examine the lamp:** A DC 15 Arcana check reveals the storm-stone inside. Its dead lightning is dangerous near metal.

**Scene 2: The Storm-stone Vault.**
- A treasure room of storm-stones. Picking one up requires a DC 13 Dexterity check. On a failure, it discharges (3d8 lightning damage).
- A Storm-stone Golem guards the vault (Appendix A).

pages.title: Session 17A: The Ironhorn Camp
pages.body:
**SAY (the Ironhorn camp):**
> "The tents are white, with horse-skulls on their poles. Drums beat slow and steady. Riders cross the camp at a gallop, shouting names you do not know. The air smells of smoke and horse-sweat and something sharp like lightning. A huge man with braids of bronze wire rises from a fire and grins at you."

**Scene 1: Yenna Garrow.** The rider with the red horse-skull takes the lamp. She weeps, and she thanks the party. If they tell her what the ghost said, she gives them something in return: a horse, or a bow, or a bargain with her clan.

**Scene 2: Thane Oru Kessa (H-06, H-21).**

> **SAY (Kessa):** "Welcome, rider. You've carried a dead man's lamp into my camp. That makes you my guests, and my guests win a wager or buy their dinner. I'll give you a steppe contest. Win, and you may speak to my council about the Court. Lose, and you'll leave me something to melt."

- **The contest:** a skill challenge. Three successes before three failures. Each player makes at most one check, using Athletics, Animal Handling, or Performance (DC 14). If the players run out of checks before the count is decided, the contest is lost.
- **If they win:** Kessa is honest. He keeps his word and opens his Tongue-Hall.
- **If they lose:** Kessa takes one weapon, and it is melted for bronze. The Tongue-Hall stays closed to them. Kessa's champion, an Ironhorn Champion, fights if the party tries to take the Tongue by force.

**Scene 3: The Real Offer.**

> **SAY (Kessa, in private):** "I'm dying, rider. Thrane's Tongue has been eating my hands since I took it from the Brass Road. I've heard the Court's Key can cure lightning-sickness. I don't want to die in a tent with a headache. I want to ring that bell and bring the storms back. I want Maudrin Vesk's head on a spear. Help me with one, and I'll help you with the rest. That's a fair bargain, isn't it?"

**IF THEY…**
- **…accept:** Kessa gives them his Tongue for the Thrane ringing. He asks for an oath that they will return it to the Tongue-Hall after. *Consequence:* The party must return Thrane's Tongue, or break their word (Bargain Log).
- **…refuse:** Kessa laughs. "Fair enough. Then we meet at the Tor, rider. I'll bring the horses."
  *Consequence:* Kessa keeps the Tongue-Hall closed. The party can take Thrane's Tongue by theft (DC 15 Stealth, past the Ironhorn riders), or Yenna Garrow can smuggle it out for a favour (DC 14 Stealth).
- **…reveal the Tongue they have:** His eyes narrow. He will take it, by force if needed or by contest if the party is clever.

pages.title: Session 18A: Corin's Workshop
pages.body:
**SAY (Corin Aldeth):**
> "Ah, you've been to Brassfall. Good. I was hoping you'd come this way. My name is Corin Aldeth. I'm a Bellwright. My family has tried to finish a song for three generations, and I think you may be the first people in a century who can help me finish it."

**Scene 1: The Workshop.**
- A hidden workshop beneath a Brassfall tavern. Bells in various stages of repair.
- Corin shows the party *Edda Thorne's Notes*, the Bellwrights' copy of the tuning pages. They describe a safe way to ring the Seventh.
- He asks for their help. He admits the Toll for the Seventh will be high.

> **SAY (Corin, on the Toll):** "Yes, there's a cost. There's always a cost. The Seventh takes everything from everyone who hears it. The Court has taken memories in small pieces for four hundred years. I'm asking you to pay for it all at once, and to get something back for it."

**IF THEY…**
- **…agree to help Corin:** He gives them the Notes and his plan. *Consequence:* The party can take the Seventh path (Part 10) with his help.
- **…refuse:** Corin is disappointed. He sends a Tongue-Hound to follow the party.
- **…argue:** Corin is passionate, not cruel. He explains his logic for hours. He is wrong, but he is not evil.

**Encounter (optional, Bellwright ambush):** Three Tongue-Hounds. If forced to fight, Corin joins at CR 5.

pages.title: Session 19A: The Storms Return
pages.body:
**Scene 1: Ringing Thrane.**
- The party rings Thrane at the Lightning Shafts. They must bring Thrane's Tongue from the Tongue-Hall.
- **Toll:** A Sense, for one day (Part 2.11). The Ringer becomes Lightning-Marked: once per day, when they take lightning damage, they may unleash 1d6 lightning on a creature within 10 feet.

> **SAY (when Thrane rings):** "The bell cracks like a whip. The sky above Brassfall splits open, and for the first time in four centuries a real storm rolls over the mountains. Rain falls like bronze filings. Lightning strikes the peaks in long white bars. The storm-stones blaze, and every metal object you carry hums in answer."

**Consequences:**
- The storms return to Brassfall. Mines become dangerous, but the ore can be recovered.
- The Ironhorn celebrate, and Kessa's sickness eases for a season.
- The Court sends a strike force of Hushmen and Dawn Order knights to take the Thrane Tongue.

pages.title: Session 16B: The Sleeping Hall
pages.body:
**SAY (arrival):**
> "The hill rises alone above the plain, ringed with grey stones. At night, faint lights move among the stones like fireflies. The air hums. From the summit, a sound like someone breathing in their sleep drifts down toward you. When you close your eyes, you dream of a room full of beds, and every bed has someone sleeping in it."

**Scene 1: The Sleepless.**
- The Sleepless emerge at night, shaped by the fears of the nearest sleeper.
- Anyone who rests on the Tor must make a DC 13 Wisdom save. On a failure, they wake with a nightmare (disadvantage on the first Insight check the next day). If they fail by 5 or more, a Sleepless takes shape.

**Encounter: Sleepless (two).**

**Scene 2: The Sleeping Hall.**
- The Hall holds hundreds of sleepers who do not wake. Mirel's bell hangs above the central bed.
- If the party holds Mirel's Tongue (from the Librarian, Session 5), they ring it at the end of Session 19B, after Corin's scene. If not, the Librarian's courier arrives at the Hall and repeats the offer: a dream for the Tongue, delivered in person. If the party refuses again, Mirel cannot be rung, and the Concord is lost.

pages.title: Session 17B: The Hush Cult
pages.body:
**SAY (the Hush Cult):**
> "A group of robed figures sits in a circle around a dying fire, humming very softly. When they see you, they smile, and their smile is sad and kind and terribly tired. *'Rest, friends,'* one says. *'You're so tired. Why not rest here, where the song is kind?'*"

**Scene 1: The Cult's Offer.**
- The Cult offers rest, dreamless sleep, and an end to the Sleepless, in exchange for one night by the Hush Shrine.
- If the party sleeps there, the Hush takes a dream from each of them. A character who loses a dream cannot dream again until the Hush is struck or sealed (Session 26).

**IF THEY…**
- **…refuse and attack:** The Cult defends the shrine. **Encounter:** Hush Cultists (four) and a Cult Leader.
- **…accept and sleep:** Their dreams are taken. Describe the emptiness. The Hush begins to stir.

pages.title: Session 18B: The Shrine's Stairs and Corin
pages.body:
**SAY (the stairs):**
> "The stairs spiral down into the hill, each step worn smooth by feet that came to listen. Your footsteps are muffled, though the stone is bare. At the bottom a great bell hangs in darkness, its surface blank as a sleeping face. Under the lullaby, very faintly, something breathes."

**Scene 1: The Hush Shrine (Visit Only).**
- The party may descend a few steps. They will hear the Hush, but they cannot ring Ysh without the Key.
- The Hush speaks in the voice of the listener's sleeping self.

> **SAY (the Hush):** "Be quiet now. You're so close. I've held everything together for four hundred years, and I'm so tired. If you wake me, the dream will end. Do you want that? Do you want the world to end because you couldn't keep your mouth shut?"

**Scene 2: Corin Arrives.** Corin comes up the stairs, wanting Mirel rung to weaken the Tor's defences. He wants the party to help him ring Ysh later.

> **SAY (Corin):** "Mirel first. Mirel is the lullaby's mother. Ring her, and the Seventh's voice will carry. Ring her wrong, and the Hush will sing you to sleep before the Court can arrest you. I know how the bells work. My grandmother rang one. Let me help you do it right."

pages.title: Session 19B: Mirel's Ringing
pages.body:
**Scene 1: Ringing Mirel.**
- The Ringer stands at the Sleeping Hall's bell with Mirel's Tongue.
- **Toll:** A Fear, chosen by the player, lost for one day (Part 2.7).

> **SAY (when Mirel rings):** "The bell sings like a lullaby sung by someone who loves you. Every sleeper on the Tor sighs and turns over. The Sleepless dissolve into mist. For a moment the air feels like the first morning of spring, and you feel, impossibly, hopeful."

**Consequences:**
- The Sleepless stop walking.
- The Hush's lullaby changes key, and it sounds sad, then grateful.
- The Court sends Hushmen to the Tor to investigate.

pages.title: THE SECOND BRANCH (Sessions 20 and 21, Compressed)
pages.body:
**Session 20: The Second Arrival.** Run the first scene of the second branch. For each skipped scene, give one clue: for Brassfall, the lamp's storm-stone and the Tongue-Hall; for the Tor, the Hush Cult's offer and Corin's warning that Mirel comes first.

**Session 21: The Second Ringing.** Run the second branch's ringing and its Toll. Give one more clue: Maudrin has marched on the Tor, and the Key rides with her. The second ringing sets the Strike in motion (Session 23).

**If the party has rung both bells:** The Court's strike force is already moving. Session 22 begins at dusk.

pages.title: Session 22: The Truth of the Key
pages.body:
**Scene 1: Edda Thorne's Notes.** The party reads Edda's tuning pages, from Corin, the Librarian, or the diary (if they took it in Session 5). The pages tell the story of the Quiet Night, in Edda's own words. If none of the three sources is available, the Librarian reads the Quiet Night page aloud for one true memory:

> **SAY (read aloud, from Edda's Notes):** "He wants to tune the seven into one long spring. I told him the seventh is not a bell. It is the lullaby. The Key is not a tuning tool. It is the tongue that sings Oum to sleep, and he has taken it to make the calendar behave. If he strikes the Seventh with it, the dream will wake or it will crack. I told him so. He did not hear me."

**Scene 2: What the Key Is.** Pieced together, the party now understands:

- The Seventh bell keeps Oum asleep.
- The Key is the Seventh's Tongue, and the only tongue that can ring it.
- Imber struck the Key against the bells on the Quiet Night, and the discord cracked the lullaby. The bells went silent because the dream was waking.
- Maudrin has known this since she took the Key, and she has kept it from the Court and the Church alike. It is not about tuning. It is about keeping the lullaby as it is.

**Scene 3: Maudrin Is Moving.** Word reaches the party that Maudrin has left Hallowmere with an army of Hushmen and Dawn Order knights. She carries the Key in a silence-stone case on a chain around her neck.

**Scene 4: The Allies Gather.** Ask each player which ally they want to bring, and which ones they trust:

- **Dawn Order** (if Rook won the duel): Rook and her knights, who hold the ridge in the Strike and take one Hushman off the line.
- **Bellwrights** (if they trust the party): Corin's workshop, the Tongue-Hounds, and the Notes.
- **Ironhorn** (if Kessa survived): Yenna Garrow and her riders.
- **Drowned Choir** (if Ossa was rung): the Cantor sings for them.
- **Stilled** (if they thawed Glassreach): they walk.
- **Blanks** (if they helped in Session 7): they march.
- **Ilam Bray** (if reunited with Jonah): he holds the Tor's southern road. Each ally has one more action: Yenna Garrow's riders cut off the Hushmen's retreat; the Cantor sings at the summit, and allies gain advantage on saves against fear; the Stilled stand in the Strike as living walls; the Blanks break the Hushmen's line by numbers.

pages.title: Session 23: The Strike
pages.body:
**SAY (the Strike):**
> "Hushmen on grey horses come over the ridge in a long line. Their gloves catch the light and throw it back as silence. Behind them rides a figure in dove-grey, white-haired, with a face you have seen in your dreams. *'Good evening,'* Maudrin Vesk says, her voice carrying perfectly over the wind. *'I'm so sorry to interrupt. But I believe you have something that belongs to me.'*"

**Scene 1: The Strike.**
- Maudrin commands four Hushmen, two Dawn Order knights, and Ser Haldric Mose.
- She wants the Tongues the party carries, and she wants the Key back in her hands if the party has it. She offers: surrender the Tongues and be spared, or fight.
- **If the party still owes Maudrin the favour from Session 4:** She calls the favour in: "One favour, dear, and I am calling it in now. Go, before I change my mind." If the favour was already repaid or never owed, she says "You have repaid me. Go," and runs the Strike normally.

**IF THEY…**
- **…surrender:** Maudrin takes the Tongues, and the Key too if the party holds it. She then demands the party's Ringer come with her to the Quiet Court to be Tithed. The Ringer must resist with a DC 15 Charisma save, or accept the Tithe. If the Ringer accepts the Tithe, skip Session 24 and go straight to the Empty Choir (Part 10). If the Ringer resists, the Strike continues into the reeds.
- **…fight:** Use the Strike encounter. Maudrin retreats at half HP toward the Tor, saying: "I'll see you at the Shrine." She keeps the Key.
- **…steal the Key during the fight:** To take the case, a character who reaches Maudrin makes a DC 16 Sleight of Hand check after she has been struck once. On failure, the Key stays with her and she retreats to the summit. On success, the party holds the Key, the best outcome for the Second Dawn, the Concord, or the Unbound. Haldric, who did not know the Key was real, sees it in the party's hands and hesitates. That hesitation breaks the Court's line.

**Encounter: The Strike (Appendix A).** Four Hushmen, two Dawn Order Knights, Ser Haldric Mose, and Maudrin Vesk. Deadly for levels 7 to 9. If Rook won the duel, Haldric and both Knights are absent, which makes it Hard.

**Scene 2: Jonah.** If Ilam has Jonah, Ilam stays between the boy and the fight. Jonah sees his father clearly, for the first time since the Court took his father's memory. If the party left Jonah in Court custody, Maudrin brings him to the ridge as a hostage, and freeing him costs one Tongue or the Strike.

**Session 23 end:** The party reaches the foot of the Tor. Ahead, a ring of grey stones glows, and the light is the colour of a dream they have almost forgotten.

---

pages.title: ACT V: THE SEVENTH BELL (Levels 10 to 11, Sessions 24 to 30)
pages.body:
**Goal:** Reach the summit. Defeat or outwit Maudrin Vesk. Take the Key. Descend the Hush Shrine. Decide what to do with the Seventh Bell.

**Central location:** Vael Tor, and the Hush Shrine beneath it.

**The state of play before Session 24** determines which endings are open. Check the Canon Sheet and the Ring Table, and record:

- **Which bells were rung?** Vaer, Ossa, Calla, Hieme, Thrane, Mirel. The Concord needs all six.
- **Who holds the Key?** Maudrin, or the party.
- **Did Rook win the duel? Is Maudrin's Session 4 favour still owed?** Both affect Haldric and the Strike.

pages.title: Session 24: The Summit
pages.body:
**SAY (the summit):**
> "The stones of the Tor stand in a ring. In the centre, Maudrin Vesk waits with her Hushmen in a silent line. Behind her, the ground opens onto a spiral of stairs. The Hush rises from below like a tide, a lullaby so vast and low you feel it in your ribs. *'I'm glad you came,'* Maudrin says. *'Shall we begin?'*"

**Scene 1: Maudrin's Last Stand.**
- If Maudrin still holds the Key, she fights to slow the party, and retreats down the stairs at half HP. She intends to ring the Seventh herself.
- If the party holds the Key, Maudrin negotiates. She has nothing left to bargain with, and she knows it.

> **SAY (Maudrin, final conversation):** "I'm not your enemy. I'm the last person in Corvane who understands what the silence costs. Four centuries of Tithes. Blanks. Children who forget their mothers. And you want to wake the thing that holds it all together? You're mad, or you're brave. I've never been able to tell the difference."

**Encounter: Maudrin Vesk (CR 6).** Use only if Maudrin holds the Key; otherwise run her negotiation. She fights with *Silence* and *Counterspell*. At half HP, she retreats down the stairs with the Key.

pages.title: Session 25: The Stairs of the Hush
pages.body:
**SAY (the descent):**
> "The stairs go on for a long time. Each step has a memory carved into it, worn smooth by the feet of those who came to listen. Some are your memories. Some are strangers'. You hear a child laughing, a bell tolling, a man telling a joke to someone who isn't there. At the bottom, a great bell hangs in darkness."

**Scene 1: The Toll of the Stairs (H-24).**
- Each character who descends pays one memory every twenty steps: five memories each across the 100 steps. Allies pay the same.
- A DC 13 Wisdom save halves the cost.
- Allies who descend with the party pay too. Some may refuse, and that is an emotional beat.

**DO:** Keep this scene moving. Narrate the memories being lost without listing them. Let each player name one memory and cross it off.

pages.title: Session 26: The Seventh Bell
pages.body:
**The scene depends on who holds the Key.**

**IF MAUDRIN HOLDS THE KEY:**

> **SAY:** "The bell is vast and blank, its surface like the face of a sleeping god. Maudrin stands before it, the Key raised. *'I'm sorry,'* she says. *'But I've made my choice.'* She strikes the Key against the bell, once. The sound is a sigh so deep it seems to come from the foundations of the world. The lullaby stutters. Something beneath the Tor stirs."

- The Hush cracks. Oum begins to wake. This is Path 2, the Hush Unbound. The party can still intervene, but only by destroying Maudrin, which cannot stop the sound.

**IF THE PARTY HOLDS THE KEY:**

> **SAY:** "The bell is vast and blank, its surface like the face of a sleeping god. You stand before it with the Key in your hands. Maudrin, behind you, has nothing left, and she is weeping. The lullaby is still there, very faint, asking you to be quiet. Your choice is the only one left in the world."

- The figure from Session 11's winter-moment stands at the bell's foot: the character, older, holding the Key, and smiling. Ask the player what they feel, and do not explain it.
- Before any strike, whoever rings the Seventh pays all six Tolls (Part 2.11), Maudrin included.
- The party chooses, and the endings open. See Session 27.
